header_chirho: For God so loved the world that he gave his only begotten Son, that whoever believes in him should not perish but have eternal life. - John 3:16
tagline_chirho: A drop-in Linux-compatible kernel rewritten in Rust, for safety, for performance, for glory.

vision_chirho.summary_chirho: Lineluya is a ground-up rewrite of the Linux kernel in Rust, designed to be binary-compatible and drop-in swappable with the real Linux kernel. It implements the Linux syscall ABI, boot protocols, filesystem interfaces (/proc, /sys, /dev), and module system so that existing Linux userspace (init, coreutils, systemd, containers, etc.) runs unmodified.
goals_chirho: Full Linux x86_64 syscall ABI compatibility — existing ELF binaries run unmodified
Linux boot protocol support (bzImage format, loadable by GRUB2/systemd-boot/Limine)
Memory safety via Rust's ownership model — eliminate classes of CVEs (buffer overflows, use-after-free, data races)
Performance parity with Linux (within 5% on macro benchmarks)
ELF binary loading with dynamic linker support
Loadable kernel module system (Rust modules, with C ABI shim layer for legacy .ko)
Full networking stack (TCP/IP, UDP, socket API)
Modern filesystem support (ext4, tmpfs, procfs, sysfs, devtmpfs)
Eventually: full Linux ecosystem rewrite (coreutils, systemd, drivers) in Rust
non_goals_chirho: Supporting architectures other than x86_64 in Phase 1 (ARM64, RISC-V come later)
100% driver coverage from day one (focus on virtio, essential hardware first)
Supporting 32-bit userspace (x86 compat mode) in early phases

key_reference_projects_chirho.relevance_chirho: MOST RELEVANT — Rust framekernel with 230+ Linux syscalls, only ~14% unsafe code via OSTD framework. Linux ABI compatible. On par with Linux in benchmarks. Published at USENIX ATC 2025. Has experimental NixOS distribution. Accepted to USENIX ATC'25.
key_reference_projects_chirho.architecture_chirho: Framekernel: single address space (monolithic performance) with logical separation between privileged OS framework (OSTD, only unsafe Rust allowed) and de-privileged OS services (safe Rust only). Combines monolithic kernel performance with microkernel security properties.
key_reference_projects_chirho.key_lesson_chirho: Demonstrates that minimizing unsafe to a well-defined framework layer (~14%) is achievable while supporting 230+ syscalls at Linux-competitive performance.

key_reference_projects_chirho.relevance_chirho: Rust kernel explicitly targeting Linux compatibility. 135/437 syscalls implemented (~31%). Can run Bash + musl libc. Started as C (2018), rewritten in Rust after 1.5 years -- validates Rust rewrite approach. 48,800 lines of Rust across 615 files. Boots via Multiboot2.
key_reference_projects_chirho.key_lesson_chirho: Shows the difficulty curve: 135 syscalls is enough for a basic shell but not for a full distribution. The C-to-Rust rewrite history demonstrates that Rust improves kernel code maintainability significantly.

key_reference_projects_chirho.relevance_chirho: Mature Rust microkernel OS. NOT Linux-compatible but has excellent Rust kernel engineering patterns. Uses scheme-based resource model (URLs instead of file paths). Syscall performance optimized to near-CPU-microcode overhead. Self-hosting. Custom relibc.
key_reference_projects_chirho.key_lesson_chirho: Demonstrates that Rust kernel syscall dispatch can be made extremely fast. The scheme system is elegant but incompatible with Linux's VFS model. Their dedicated syscall crate with inline ASM wrappers is a good pattern.

key_reference_projects_chirho.relevance_chirho: Research OS exploring intralingual design: encoding OS invariants as Rust types checked at compile time. Single address space (ring 0 only), isolation via type system not hardware. 38,000 lines Rust + 900 lines ASM. Published at USENIX OSDI'20.
key_reference_projects_chirho.key_lesson_chirho: Innovative idea of encoding invariants as types (e.g., MappedPageChirho can only exist when page is actually mapped). However, SASOS is incompatible with Linux's kernel/user separation. Applicable insight: use Rust types to prevent page table bugs at compile time.

key_reference_projects_chirho.relevance_chirho: Rust is now permanent in the Linux kernel (2025 Kernel Maintainer Summit). kernel crate provides safe abstractions; bindings crate has auto-generated C FFI. Millions of Android 16 devices use Rust kernel code in production. DRM subsystem adoption advancing.
key_reference_projects_chirho.key_lesson_chirho: The kernel crate's abstraction patterns (error types, lock guards, device model traits) are excellent design references even though they wrap C code. Shows which abstractions work well for kernel Rust.

key_reference_projects_chirho.relevance_chirho: Monolithic Rust kernel with Linux binary compatibility. Can run unmodified Linux binaries. Good syscall implementation reference.
Rust library that parses and loads Linux kernels from bzImage format. Contains Rust implementation of boot_params parsing. Directly useful for understanding how to produce a compatible bzImage.
4-stage x86/x86_64 chain loader written in Rust. Demonstrates real mode -> protected mode -> long mode transition in Rust/asm. Reference for Lineluya's boot stub.

syscall_entry_mechanism_chirho.msr_lstar_chirho: MSR 0xC0000082 -- holds kernel entry point address (entry_SYSCALL_64)
syscall_entry_mechanism_chirho.msr_star_chirho: MSR 0xC0000081 -- holds CS/SS selectors: bits 47:32=kernel CS, bits 63:48=user CS
syscall_entry_mechanism_chirho.msr_syscall_mask_chirho: MSR 0xC0000084 -- RFLAGS mask (clears IF, DF, TF, AC)

register_abi_chirho.r10_chirho: arg3 (NOT rcx -- SYSCALL clobbers rcx with return RIP)

entry_sequence_chirho: 1. SYSCALL transitions CPU to ring 0, loads RIP from MSR_LSTAR
2. SWAPGS -- switch GS base to kernel per-CPU data
3. Save user RSP to per-CPU scratch (tss.sp2)
4. SWITCH_TO_KERNEL_CR3 (for KPTI: switch to kernel page tables)
5. Load kernel stack from per-CPU current_top_of_stack
6. Push pt_regs: SS, RSP, RFLAGS, CS, RIP, orig_rax, then all GPRs
7. Call do_syscall_64(regs, nr) -- the Rust dispatch function
8. Return via SYSRET (fast, if pt_regs unmodified) or IRET (slow, if signals/ptrace)

how_grub2_loads_linux_chirho: 1. GRUB reads the first 8KB of the kernel file (boot sector + setup sectors)
2. GRUB checks for 'HdrS' magic at offset 0x202
3. GRUB reads protocol version from offset 0x206
4. GRUB fills in boot_params fields: type_of_loader, cmd_line_ptr, ramdisk_image/size
5. GRUB loads protected-mode kernel to address specified (>= 0x100000)
6. GRUB loads initrd to address within ramdisk range
7. GRUB copies E820 memory map into boot_params.e820_table
8. GRUB transitions to protected mode (or long mode for 64-bit) and jumps to code32_start
9. The kernel's startup stub receives pointer to boot_params in ESI register

elf_loading_deep_dive_chirho.description_chirho: ELF binary loading process from Linux 6.19.8 fs/binfmt_elf.c
load_steps_chirho: 1. Validate ELF header: magic 0x7f454c46, class ELFCLASS64, data ELFDATA2LSB, type ET_EXEC or ET_DYN
2. Read program headers from e_phoff, validate e_phnum and e_phentsize
3. If PT_INTERP exists, read interpreter path (typically /lib64/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2)
4. flush_old_exec: destroy old address space, reset signals
5. For each PT_LOAD: mmap the segment at p_vaddr (with load_bias for PIE/ET_DYN), permissions from p_flags
6. Zero BSS (memory between p_filesz and p_memsz within each PT_LOAD)
7. Set mm->start_code, end_code, start_data, end_data, start_brk, brk from loaded segments
8. If dynamic: load ld-linux.so via load_elf_interp() at a separate address
9. Set up user stack: push random bytes, platform strings, env strings, arg strings
10. create_elf_tables(): push auxv, envp array, argv array, argc onto stack (see layout below)
11. Entry point = interpreter entry (dynamic) or e_entry (static), stored in regs->ip

vdso_chirho.description_chirho: The kernel maps a Virtual DSO (vDSO) into every process at AT_SYSINFO_EHDR. It contains user-accessible implementations of clock_gettime, gettimeofday, time, getcpu that read kernel-maintained data pages without a full syscall.
vdso_chirho.implementation_note_chirho: Lineluya must provide a vDSO. Without it, every clock_gettime() call becomes a full syscall which severely impacts performance. The vDSO is a small ELF shared object compiled into the kernel image.

technical_challenges_chirho.description_chirho: Low-level hardware access, raw pointer manipulation, inline assembly, and memory-mapped I/O inherently require unsafe Rust. The goal is to minimize unsafe surface area by wrapping unsafe operations in safe abstractions.
technical_challenges_chirho.strategy_chirho: Follow the 'unsafe sandwich' pattern: unsafe primitives at the bottom, safe API on top. Every unsafe block gets a SAFETY comment. Use Rust's type system (PhantomData, lifetimes, pin) to encode invariants.

technical_challenges_chirho.description_chirho: Linux's C code is heavily optimized over 30+ years. Rust adds bounds checking, may have different memory layout, and the borrow checker can prevent some optimizations.
technical_challenges_chirho.strategy_chirho: Use #[inline], avoid unnecessary allocations, use zero-cost abstractions. Profile early and often. For hot paths, use unsafe optimizations where Rust's safety guarantees add measurable overhead.

technical_challenges_chirho.description_chirho: Linux has ~15 million lines of driver code. Rewriting all drivers is impractical.
technical_challenges_chirho.strategy_chirho: Phase 1: VirtIO drivers (block, net, console) for QEMU testing. Phase 2: Essential bare-metal drivers (AHCI, NVMe, Intel NIC). Phase 3: C ABI shim layer to load existing Linux .ko modules. Phase 4: Gradually rewrite popular drivers in Rust.

technical_challenges_chirho.description_chirho: Linux guarantees userspace ABI stability ('we don't break userspace'). Our kernel must match this exactly.
technical_challenges_chirho.strategy_chirho: Use Linux's own uapi headers as the source of truth. Auto-generate Rust struct definitions from Linux header files. Comprehensive test suite comparing our syscall behavior to Linux.

technical_challenges_chirho.description_chirho: Linux uses spinlocks, RCU, per-CPU variables, seqlocks, and other concurrency primitives. Rust's ownership model is different.
technical_challenges_chirho.strategy_chirho: Implement spinlock, mutex, rwlock, RCU in Rust with proper Send/Sync bounds. Use Rust's type system to prevent deadlocks at compile time where possible. Per-CPU variables via custom allocator.

Implement 4-level x86_64 page table management: PML4, PDPT, PD, PT. map_page_chirho(virt, phys, flags): map virtual to physical. unmap_page_chirho(virt): remove mapping. translate_chirho(virt): walk page tables to get physical address. Write to VGA text buffer at 0xB8000 (mapped in higher half). 80x25 character grid, each entry 2 bytes (char + attribute). Implement print! macro for VGA output. Support scrolling, cursor position, basic colors. This provides visual output when serial is not available.

Create xtask command to build kernel and launch in QEMU. cargo xtask run: build kernel ELF, create bootable image (ISO or direct -kernel flag), launch qemu-system-x86_64 with appropriate flags (-serial stdio, -display none for CI, -m 256M). Support debug mode with GDB stub (-s -S).
acceptance_criteria_chirho: cargo xtask run launches QEMU with kernel

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Create the core TaskChirho struct equivalent to Linux task_struct. Must include: pid, tgid, state (Running/Ready/Blocked/Zombie), saved register context (struct PtRegsChirho), kernel stack pointer, pointer to MmChirho (memory descriptor), parent/children links, exit code. Use Arc<SpinLock<TaskChirho>> for shared ownership. Store in a global BTreeMap<PidChirho, Arc<TaskChirho>>.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: TaskChirho struct compiles with all required fields
PID allocator assigns unique monotonic PIDs
Can create a TaskChirho for the init/idle kernel thread
Global task list accessible via TASK_LIST_CHIRHO

implementation_tasks_chirho.title_chirho: Define PtRegsChirho struct for saved CPU state
implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Create PtRegsChirho matching the Linux pt_regs layout exactly (same offsets). Fields: r15, r14, r13, r12, rbp, rbx, r11, r10, r9, r8, rax, rcx, rdx, rsi, rdi, orig_rax, rip, cs, rflags, rsp, ss. This struct is pushed onto the kernel stack on syscall/interrupt entry. Must be #[repr(C)] to match assembly expectations.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: PtRegsChirho is #[repr(C)] with correct field order
size_of::<PtRegsChirho>() matches Linux pt_regs size (168 bytes)
offset_of! for each field matches Linux offsets

implementation_tasks_chirho.title_chirho: Implement per-CPU data structure and SWAPGS support
implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Set up a per-CPU data area accessible via GS segment base. On syscall entry, SWAPGS switches from user GS to kernel GS base which points to PerCpuChirho struct containing: current task pointer, kernel stack top, scratch space for user RSP, CPU id, TSS pointer. Use WRMSRL to set MSR_GS_BASE and MSR_KERNEL_GS_BASE.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: SWAPGS correctly switches GS base between user and kernel
current_task_chirho() returns pointer to running TaskChirho
Kernel stack top readable from per-CPU data after SWAPGS

implementation_tasks_chirho.title_chirho: Set up GDT with user-mode segments (ring 3 CS/DS)
implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Extend the existing GDT to include user-mode code segment (CS, ring 3, long mode) and user-mode data segment (DS, ring 3). The STAR MSR expects kernel CS at GDT index for SYSCALL and user CS at index for SYSRET. Typical layout: null, kernel CS (0x08), kernel DS (0x10), user DS (0x1B), user CS (0x23). Note SYSRET loads CS from STAR[63:48]+16 and SS from STAR[63:48]+8, so user DS must precede user CS in GDT.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: GDT has valid user CS and DS entries at correct indices
STAR MSR configured to select correct kernel/user segments
User CS is 64-bit code segment with DPL=3
User DS is data segment with DPL=3

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Write MSRs to enable SYSCALL instruction: MSR_STAR (0xC0000081) with kernel CS in bits 47:32 and user CS base in bits 63:48. MSR_LSTAR (0xC0000082) with address of syscall_entry_chirho assembly stub. MSR_SFMASK (0xC0000084) with RFLAGS mask (clear IF, DF, TF, AC = 0x47700). Also set EFER.SCE (bit 0) to enable SYSCALL/SYSRET.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: MSR_STAR set with correct segment selectors

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Write x86_64 assembly (using Rust global_asm! or .S file) for the SYSCALL entry point. Sequence: SWAPGS, save user RSP to per-CPU scratch, load kernel RSP from per-CPU data, push full pt_regs frame (ss, rsp, rflags from r11, cs, rip from rcx, orig_rax, then all GPRs), call do_syscall_64_chirho(regs_ptr, syscall_nr) in Rust. Must handle the fact that SYSCALL clobbers RCX (with return RIP) and R11 (with RFLAGS).
acceptance_criteria_chirho: SYSCALL from user mode enters kernel handler correctly
All registers saved in PtRegsChirho on kernel stack
User RSP preserved in per-CPU scratch then pt_regs
No register corruption on entry path

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Write assembly for returning from syscall to user mode. Fast path (SYSRET): restore GPRs from pt_regs, load return RIP into RCX, load RFLAGS into R11, restore user RSP, SWAPGS, SYSRET. Slow path (IRET): needed when pt_regs modified by signals/ptrace -- push SS, RSP, RFLAGS, CS, RIP onto stack, IRETQ. Must validate user CS/RIP before SYSRET (SYSRET with non-canonical RIP causes #GP in ring 0 -- this is a known x86 errata/security issue).
acceptance_criteria_chirho: SYSRET returns to user mode with correct RIP, RSP, RFLAGS
IRET fallback works when pt_regs are modified
Non-canonical RIP detected and handled via IRET instead of SYSRET
SWAPGS executed before return to user

implementation_tasks_chirho.title_chirho: Implement syscall dispatch table and do_syscall_64_chirho
implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Create the Rust syscall dispatch function do_syscall_64_chirho(regs: &mut PtRegsChirho, nr: u64). Build a static array SYSCALL_TABLE_CHIRHO of function pointers indexed by syscall number. Look up nr in table, call handler with args extracted from regs (rdi, rsi, rdx, r10, r8, r9). Store return value in regs.rax. Return -ENOSYS for unimplemented syscalls. Table size should be 512 to cover all x86_64 syscalls.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: Syscall number dispatches to correct handler function
Arguments extracted from correct registers per ABI
Syscall number bounds checking prevents OOB access

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Implement write(fd, buf, count). For Phase 2, only support fd=1 (stdout) and fd=2 (stderr) writing to serial console. Validate user pointer buf is in user address space (< 0x0000_8000_0000_0000). Copy bytes from user memory to kernel buffer, then write to serial. Return number of bytes written or -EFAULT for bad pointer, -EBADF for unsupported fd.

Implement exit_group(status). Terminate all threads in the thread group and clean up. For Phase 2 with single-threaded processes: mark task as Zombie, store exit code, free user page tables, remove from scheduler run queue, schedule next task. If no tasks remain, halt the system (or enter idle loop).
acceptance_criteria_chirho: Process marked as Zombie after exit_group
Task removed from scheduler run queue
Exit status stored for parent to collect
System does not crash when last user process exits

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Implement brk(addr). Manages the program break (end of data segment / heap). If addr is 0, return current brk. If addr > current brk, expand heap by mapping new pages (MAP_ANONYMOUS, PROT_READ|PROT_WRITE). If addr < current brk, shrink by unmapping pages. Update mm.brk_chirho. The initial brk is set from the ELF's end of data segment (rounded up to page boundary).
acceptance_criteria_chirho: brk(0) returns current program break address
brk(higher_addr) expands heap, maps new pages
Returns new brk on success, old brk on failure

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Implement mmap(addr, length, prot, flags, fd, offset). For Phase 2, support MAP_ANONYMOUS | MAP_PRIVATE only (no file-backed mappings). Allocate physical frames, map into user page tables at requested or chosen virtual address. Handle MAP_FIXED (must use exact addr). Support PROT_READ, PROT_WRITE, PROT_EXEC flags. Track mappings in MmChirho's VMA list.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: Anonymous private mappings allocate and map physical frames
MAP_FIXED places mapping at exact address
Without MAP_FIXED, kernel chooses suitable address
VMA created and inserted into process VMA list

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Implement mprotect(addr, len, prot). Change page protection flags on existing mappings. Walk the VMA list to find affected VMAs, split VMAs if the range partially overlaps. Update page table entries with new permission bits (Present, Writable, NoExecute, User). Flush TLB for affected pages.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: Page table entries updated with new permissions
VMA split correctly when range partially overlaps
Returns 0 on success, -EINVAL for bad alignment, -ENOMEM for VMA issues

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Implement munmap(addr, length). Unmap pages from the process address space. Remove page table entries, free physical frames, remove or split affected VMAs. Flush TLB. addr must be page-aligned.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: Page table entries removed for unmapped range
Physical frames freed back to allocator
VMA removed or split as needed
Returns 0 on success, -EINVAL for bad alignment

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Implement arch_prctl(code, addr). Used by glibc/musl to set FS and GS segment bases for thread-local storage (TLS). Support ARCH_SET_FS (0x1002) to set FS base via WRFSBASE or MSR_FS_BASE, and ARCH_GET_FS (0x1003) to read it. ARCH_SET_GS (0x1001) and ARCH_GET_GS (0x1004) also needed but less common. Validate addr is canonical.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: ARCH_SET_FS sets FS base register for current task
FS base restored on context switch

implementation_tasks_chirho.title_chirho: Create user-mode page tables (separate from kernel)
implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Create a separate PML4 page table hierarchy for user processes. Map kernel space (upper half, 0xFFFF_8000_0000_0000+) identically in all user page tables (shared kernel mappings). User space occupies lower half (0x0000_0000_0000_0000 to 0x0000_7FFF_FFFF_FFFF). Implement clone_kernel_page_tables_chirho() that creates a new PML4 with kernel entries copied. User entries start empty and are populated by mmap/ELF loader.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: User page table created with kernel half shared
User half initially empty (no user mappings)
Can map pages into user space with User flag set
CR3 switch to user page table works without triple fault
Kernel code/data still accessible after CR3 switch

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Create MmChirho struct (equivalent to mm_struct) that holds: pgd (PML4 physical address for CR3), list of VmaChirho entries (sorted by start address), brk, start_code, end_code, start_data, end_data, start_stack, total mapped pages. Each TaskChirho gets its own MmChirho (or shares with threads). Implement mm_create_chirho() and mm_destroy_chirho().
acceptance_criteria_chirho: MmChirho created with empty VMA list and new page tables
mm_destroy_chirho frees all VMAs, page tables, and physical frames
VMA list maintained in sorted order by start address
brk and segment boundaries tracked correctly

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Parse static ELF64 binaries. Read and validate ELF header (magic, ELFCLASS64, ET_EXEC, EM_X86_64). Parse program headers to find PT_LOAD segments. Extract: entry point (e_entry), program header table location, each PT_LOAD segment's p_vaddr, p_memsz, p_filesz, p_offset, p_flags. Reject dynamic ELFs (those with PT_INTERP) for now.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: Correctly parses ELF64 header and validates magic/class/type
Extracts all PT_LOAD segments with addresses, sizes, permissions
Rejects non-x86_64 and non-static ELF files with clear error
No unsafe memory access during parsing

implementation_tasks_chirho.title_chirho: Implement ELF segment loader (map PT_LOAD into user memory)
implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: For each PT_LOAD segment: allocate physical frames, map at p_vaddr in user page tables with permissions from p_flags (PF_R->PROT_READ, PF_W->PROT_WRITE, PF_X->PROT_EXEC). Copy p_filesz bytes from ELF data to mapped memory. Zero remaining bytes (p_memsz - p_filesz) for BSS. Create VMA entries for each loaded segment. Set mm.start_code, end_code, start_data, end_data from segment addresses.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: PT_LOAD segments mapped at correct virtual addresses
File data copied correctly into mapped pages
BSS region zeroed (between filesz and memsz)
Page permissions match ELF segment flags
VMAs created for all loaded segments

implementation_tasks_chirho.title_chirho: Set up user stack with argc, argv, envp, auxv
implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Allocate user stack pages (e.g., 8MB at top of user space, grow-down). Set up initial stack contents per Linux ABI: from bottom up: argc (u64), argv[0..argc] pointers, NULL, envp[0..envc] pointers, NULL, auxiliary vector entries (AT_PAGESZ=4096, AT_ENTRY, AT_PHDR, AT_PHENT, AT_PHNUM, AT_RANDOM, AT_NULL), then string data for argv/envp above. AT_RANDOM must point to 16 random bytes on stack. RSP set to point at argc.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: User stack mapped at correct address with guard page
argc at top of stack (lowest address, pointed to by RSP)
argv pointers follow argc, terminated by NULL
envp pointers follow argv NULL, terminated by NULL
Auxiliary vector follows envp NULL, terminated by AT_NULL
String data for argv/envp above auxv

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Implement set_tid_address(tidptr). Store the clear_child_tid pointer in the task struct. When the task exits, the kernel writes 0 to this address and does a futex wake on it. For Phase 2, just store the pointer and return the current TID (= PID for single-threaded). This syscall is called very early by glibc/musl TLS initialization.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: Does not crash on NULL pointer argument

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Write assembly function switch_context_chirho(old_ctx: *mut Context, new_ctx: *const Context) that saves callee-saved registers (rbx, rbp, r12-r15, rsp) of current task into old_ctx, loads them from new_ctx, and returns. Also switch CR3 to new task's page tables if different. Save/restore x87/SSE state (FXSAVE/FXRSTOR or XSAVE/XRSTOR). This is a naked function using only inline assembly.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: Callee-saved registers saved and restored correctly
RSP switched to new task's kernel stack
CR3 switched to new task's page tables
Function returns to new task's saved RIP (via ret)

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Create a basic preemptive round-robin scheduler. Maintain a run queue (VecDeque of task references). Timer interrupt (from PIT or APIC timer) calls schedule_chirho() which: saves current task context, picks next Ready task from queue, switches context. Tasks have states: Running, Ready, Blocked, Zombie. schedule_chirho() is also called voluntarily on sys_exit and blocking operations.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: Blocked tasks not scheduled until unblocked
Idle task runs when no other tasks are ready
Context switch happens correctly between tasks

implementation_tasks_chirho.title_chirho: Implement user-to-kernel transition (ring 3 to ring 0 test)
implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Create a test that: creates user page tables, maps a small code snippet at a user address, sets up a user stack, uses IRET to jump to ring 3 user code, user code executes SYSCALL, kernel entry captures it and returns via SYSRET. This validates the entire ring 3 <-> ring 0 transition before loading real ELF binaries.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: IRET to ring 3 works (code executes in user mode)
SYSCALL from ring 3 enters kernel handler
No triple fault or GPF during transitions

implementation_tasks_chirho.title_chirho: Build static hello-world ELF test binary
implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Create a minimal static ELF64 binary (using assembly or C with musl -static) that does: mov rax, 1 (write); mov rdi, 1 (stdout); lea rsi, [msg]; mov rdx, len; syscall; mov rax, 231 (exit_group); xor rdi, rdi; syscall. Compile and embed in kernel image or load from initrd. This is THE acceptance test for Phase 2.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: Produces a valid static ELF64 x86_64 binary
readelf shows correct ELF header and PT_LOAD segments
Runs on real Linux and outputs 'Hello from Lineluya!'

implementation_tasks_chirho.title_chirho: Integrate ELF loader with task creation and run hello world
implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Wire everything together: at kernel init, create a new TaskChirho, allocate user page tables (MmChirho), load the hello world ELF binary into user memory, set up the user stack, set the task's initial RIP to ELF entry point, initial RSP to top of user stack, initial RFLAGS with IF set, set CS/SS to user segments. Add task to scheduler. Switch to it. The binary should output 'Hello from Lineluya!' to serial and exit cleanly.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: Hello world ELF binary runs to completion
'Hello from Lineluya!' appears on serial console
No kernel panic or triple fault

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Create safe helper functions for kernel to read/write user memory: copy_from_user_chirho(kernel_dst, user_src, len) and copy_to_user_chirho(user_dst, kernel_src, len). Must validate that user addresses are in user space range (canonical, below 0x0000_8000_0000_0000). Handle page faults gracefully (return -EFAULT). Optionally use STAC/CLAC (SMAP) for security.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: copy_from_user reads user memory into kernel buffer
copy_to_user writes kernel data to user memory
Non-mapped user addresses return -EFAULT (no kernel panic)
Page fault handler recognizes user access faults

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Implement exit(status). Similar to exit_group but only terminates the calling thread (not the thread group). For Phase 2 with single-threaded processes, behavior is identical to exit_group. Register in syscall table at nr=60.

Allocate a dedicated kernel stack for each task (typically 16KB or 2 pages, matching Linux THREAD_SIZE). Place a guard page below the stack to catch stack overflow. Store kernel stack top in per-CPU data for SYSCALL entry. Implement alloc_kernel_stack_chirho() and free_kernel_stack_chirho().
acceptance_criteria_chirho: Each task gets its own kernel stack
Guard page below stack causes page fault on overflow
Kernel stack top accessible from per-CPU data

implementation_tasks_chirho.title_chirho: QEMU integration test harness for Phase 2
implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Create an automated test that: builds the kernel with embedded hello world ELF, launches QEMU with -serial stdio -display none, captures serial output, checks for 'Hello from Lineluya!' string, verifies clean exit (no panic), times out after 10 seconds. Add as xtask command: cargo xtask test-phase2. Return exit code 0 on success, 1 on failure.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: cargo xtask test-phase2 runs the full test automatically
QEMU starts and captures serial output
Test passes when hello world output detected
Test fails on panic or timeout

implementation_tasks_chirho.title_chirho: Implement TSS (Task State Segment) for ring transitions
implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Configure the TSS with IST (Interrupt Stack Table) entries for double fault handler and NMI. Set RSP0 to point to current task's kernel stack top so that ring 3 -> ring 0 transitions via interrupts load the correct kernel stack. Update RSP0 on every context switch to the new task's kernel stack.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: TSS RSP0 set to current task's kernel stack
IST entries configured for double fault
Ring 3 interrupt entry loads correct kernel stack

implementation_tasks_chirho.title_chirho: Implement page fault handler for user-space faults
implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Extend the page fault handler to distinguish kernel vs user faults (check CR2 address and error code bit 2). For user-space faults: if address is in a valid VMA but page not present, allocate and map page (demand paging). If address not in any VMA, deliver SIGSEGV. If write to read-only COW page, handle copy-on-write (Phase 3). Log fault details to serial for debugging.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: User page fault on valid VMA triggers demand paging
User page fault on invalid address delivers SIGSEGV
Kernel page fault panics with diagnostic info
Error code bits parsed correctly (user/supervisor, read/write, present/not-present)

implementation_tasks_chirho.title_chirho: Implement kernel panic handler with register dump
implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Enhance panic handler to print: panic message, register dump (all GPRs, CR2, CR3, RFLAGS), stack trace (walk RBP chain), current task PID and name, backtrace with function names (if symbol table available). Halt all CPUs on panic (for future SMP). Use serial output to ensure panic info visible even if VGA broken.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: Current PID and task name shown
System halts after panic (no further execution)

implementation_tasks_chirho.title_chirho: Implement errno constants and error handling
implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Define all Linux errno constants: EPERM(1), ENOENT(2), ESRCH(3), EINTR(4), EIO(5), ..., ENOSYS(38), ..., up to ~133. Create ErrnoChirho enum with From<i64> conversion. Syscall handlers return Result<u64, ErrnoChirho>. The dispatch function converts errors to negative values in rax (Linux convention: -errno in return register).

Create a PID allocator that assigns unique PIDs. Use a bitmap or incrementing counter with recycling. Reserve PID 0 for idle/swapper, PID 1 for init. Max PID configurable (default 32768 like Linux). PID 0 is never assigned to user processes. Thread group ID (TGID) equals leader's PID.

implementation_tasks_chirho.title_chirho: Implement SpinLock and Mutex for kernel synchronization
implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Implement SpinLockChirho: busy-wait lock using atomic compare-and-swap. Disable interrupts on lock (to prevent deadlock with interrupt handlers). Implement MutexChirho: sleeping lock (blocks task if contended, for Phase 2 use SpinLock underneath). Both implement Deref/DerefMut for ergonomic access. impl Send+Sync for shared data protection.

Implement RwLockChirho: allows multiple concurrent readers or one exclusive writer. Uses atomic counter: positive = reader count, -1 = writer holds lock. Reader increments counter, writer sets to -1. Writer waits for counter to reach 0. Useful for protecting data read far more often than written (e.g., process list, mount table).
acceptance_criteria_chirho: Multiple readers can hold lock simultaneously

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Enable SMAP (Supervisor Mode Access Prevention) and SMEP (Supervisor Mode Execution Prevention) for security. SMEP: CR4 bit 20 -- prevents kernel from executing user-mapped pages (prevents ret2usr attacks). SMAP: CR4 bit 21 -- prevents kernel from accessing user-mapped pages except via explicit STAC/CLAC. Check CPUID for support before enabling. copy_from/to_user must use STAC/CLAC when SMAP enabled.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: SMEP enabled if CPU supports it
SMAP enabled if CPU supports it
Kernel page fault on direct user access with SMAP

implementation_tasks_chirho.title_chirho: Define VFS trait hierarchy (InodeOpsChirho, FileOpsChirho, SuperOpsChirho)
implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Create Rust traits for the VFS abstraction layer. InodeOpsChirho: lookup, create, mkdir, unlink, rmdir, rename, readlink, getattr, setattr. FileOpsChirho: read, write, llseek, poll, ioctl, mmap, open, release, fsync, readdir. SuperOpsChirho: alloc_inode, destroy_inode, write_inode, statfs, sync_fs, put_super. DentryOpsChirho: d_compare, d_hash, d_delete. Use trait objects (dyn) for runtime polymorphism like Linux's vtable approach.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: All VFS traits defined with correct method signatures
Traits can be implemented by different filesystem types
InodeChirho, FileChirho, DentryChirho, SuperblockChirho structs hold trait objects
VFS types compile and are usable from kernel crate

implementation_tasks_chirho.title_chirho: Implement file descriptor table per process
implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Create FdTableChirho for each process. Maps file descriptor numbers (i32) to Arc<FileChirho>. Support: alloc_fd_chirho() to get lowest available fd, get_file_chirho(fd) to look up, close_fd_chirho(fd) to remove and drop. Start each process with fds 0,1,2 for stdin/stdout/stderr. Implement CLOEXEC flag tracking. Max fd configurable (default 1024, expandable).
acceptance_criteria_chirho: File lookup by fd works correctly
close removes fd and drops file reference
Each process gets its own FdTableChirho

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Implement the path resolution algorithm that walks a pathname string and resolves it to a DentryChirho/InodeChirho. Handle: absolute paths (start from root dentry), relative paths (start from cwd), '..' (parent), '.' (current), symlink following (with loop detection, max 40 symlinks like Linux), AT_FDCWD for *at() syscalls, mount point crossing (walk into mounted filesystem's root).
acceptance_criteria_chirho: Relative paths resolved from process cwd
Returns ENOENT for missing path components
Returns ENOTDIR for non-directory in path

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Implement a complete in-memory filesystem (tmpfs). All data stored in kernel heap. Support regular files (read/write with page-backed data), directories (linked list of children), symlinks, device nodes (mknod). Implement all InodeOpsChirho and FileOpsChirho methods. This is the simplest real filesystem and tests the VFS abstractions.

implementation_tasks_chirho.title_chirho: Implement mount infrastructure and root filesystem
implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Create mount infrastructure: MountChirho struct (mount point dentry, mounted filesystem superblock, flags), global mount tree, mount() syscall that creates new mount. Set up initial root filesystem as tmpfs. Implement umount2(). Support MS_BIND, MS_MOVE, MS_RDONLY flags. Track per-process root and cwd in FsStructChirho (equivalent to fs_struct).
acceptance_criteria_chirho: Root filesystem mounted as tmpfs at boot
mount() syscall mounts filesystems at mount points

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Implement procfs with key entries: /proc/self (symlink to current PID), /proc/[pid]/status, /proc/[pid]/maps, /proc/[pid]/cmdline, /proc/[pid]/comm, /proc/[pid]/fd/ (directory of symlinks), /proc/[pid]/exe (symlink), /proc/cpuinfo, /proc/meminfo, /proc/version, /proc/uptime, /proc/loadavg, /proc/filesystems, /proc/mounts, /proc/cmdline, /proc/stat. Each file generates content dynamically on read.

implementation_tasks_chirho.title_chirho: Implement devtmpfs (/dev) with essential device nodes
implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Create devtmpfs filesystem mounted at /dev with essential device nodes: /dev/null (1,3) reads return 0 bytes, writes succeed silently; /dev/zero (1,5) reads return zeroes, writes succeed silently; /dev/full (1,7) reads return zeroes, writes return -ENOSPC; /dev/random and /dev/urandom (1,8 and 1,9) return pseudorandom bytes; /dev/console (5,1), /dev/tty (5,0); symlinks /dev/stdin->/proc/self/fd/0 etc.

Implement read(fd, buf, count): look up FileChirho from fd table, call file_ops.read(), copy data to user buffer. Implement openat(dirfd, pathname, flags, mode): resolve path to inode, create FileChirho, allocate fd, handle O_CREAT, O_TRUNC, O_APPEND, O_RDONLY/O_WRONLY/O_RDWR, O_CLOEXEC, O_DIRECTORY, O_NOFOLLOW. Also implement legacy open() as openat(AT_FDCWD, ...).
acceptance_criteria_chirho: open() creates FileChirho and returns valid fd
read() reads from file and copies to user buffer
O_CREAT creates new file if not exists

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: close(fd): remove fd from table, drop file reference. dup(oldfd): allocate lowest available fd pointing to same file. dup2(oldfd, newfd): close newfd if open, point newfd to same file. dup3(oldfd, newfd, flags): like dup2 but support O_CLOEXEC flag. These are fundamental for shell I/O redirection.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: close() releases fd and drops file reference
dup() returns new fd pointing to same file
dup3() sets CLOEXEC on new fd

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Implement pipe(pipefd[2]) and pipe2(pipefd[2], flags). Create an anonymous pipe: a pair of file descriptors where writes to pipefd[1] can be read from pipefd[0]. Internal buffer (64KB like Linux default). Blocking read when empty, blocking write when full. Handle EAGAIN for O_NONBLOCK. EOF (read returns 0) when all write ends closed. SIGPIPE when writing to pipe with no readers.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: pipe() returns two valid file descriptors
Data written to write-end readable from read-end
O_NONBLOCK returns EAGAIN instead of blocking

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Implement fork() via clone() syscall. Create child TaskChirho: new PID, copy parent's register state, duplicate file descriptor table (shared Arc<FileChirho>), duplicate signal handlers. For memory: implement copy-on-write (COW) -- mark all parent/child pages as read-only, on write page fault allocate new physical frame, copy page content, remap with write permission. Clone flags: CLONE_VM (share address space, for threads), CLONE_FILES, CLONE_FS, CLONE_SIGHAND.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: fork() creates child with new PID
Write to shared page triggers copy-on-write
Child gets copy of fd table
fork() returns 0 in child, child PID in parent
CLONE_VM shares address space (for future threads)

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Implement execve(pathname, argv, envp). Replace current process image: resolve pathname to ELF binary, destroy old address space (free old VMAs and page tables), load new ELF binary (reuse Phase 2 ELF loader), set up new stack with argv/envp/auxv, close CLOEXEC file descriptors, reset signal handlers to SIG_DFL (except SIG_IGN). Entry point set to new ELF's e_entry.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: New binary loaded and replaces old process image
argv and envp accessible from new process
Returns to new entry point (does not return on success)

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Implement wait4(pid, wstatus, options, rusage). Wait for child process state change. If pid > 0, wait for specific child. If pid == -1, wait for any child. If pid == 0, wait for any child in same process group. If WNOHANG set, return immediately if no child exited. Store exit status in wstatus (encode with WIFEXITED/WEXITSTATUS macros). Reap zombie child (free task struct). Support WUNTRACED and WCONTINUED for job control.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: Parent blocks until child exits (without WNOHANG)
WNOHANG returns 0 immediately if no child exited
Exit status correctly encoded in wstatus

implementation_tasks_chirho.title_chirho: Implement stat family syscalls (stat, fstat, lstat, fstatat)
implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Implement stat(path, statbuf), fstat(fd, statbuf), lstat(path, statbuf), newfstatat(dirfd, path, statbuf, flags). Fill struct stat with: st_dev, st_ino, st_mode, st_nlink, st_uid, st_gid, st_rdev, st_size, st_blksize, st_blocks, st_atime, st_mtime, st_ctime. lstat does not follow symlinks. Struct stat must match Linux's x86_64 layout exactly.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: stat() returns correct metadata for files and directories
struct stat layout matches Linux exactly
st_mode encodes file type (S_IFREG, S_IFDIR, etc.)

implementation_tasks_chirho.title_chirho: Implement directory syscalls (mkdir, rmdir, getdents64, getcwd, chdir)
implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: mkdir(path, mode): create directory inode. rmdir(path): remove empty directory. getdents64(fd, dirp, count): fill linux_dirent64 structs with directory entries (d_ino, d_off, d_reclen, d_type, d_name). getcwd(buf, size): return current working directory path. chdir(path): change process cwd. fchdir(fd): change cwd to directory referenced by fd.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: rmdir removes empty directories (ENOTEMPTY for non-empty)
getdents64 returns directory entries in correct format
getcwd returns absolute path of current directory

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Implement ioctl(fd, request, arg) syscall with a dispatch framework. Each FileOpsChirho implementor handles its own ioctl commands. Essential ioctls: TIOCGWINSZ (get terminal window size), FIONREAD (bytes available), TCGETS/TCSETS (terminal attributes). Return -ENOTTY for unsupported ioctls on non-TTY files. Phase 3 provides the framework; TTY-specific ioctls in Phase 4.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: Framework extensible for future ioctl commands

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: lseek(fd, offset, whence): SEEK_SET sets position to offset, SEEK_CUR adds offset to current position, SEEK_END adds offset to file size. fcntl(fd, cmd, arg): F_GETFL/F_SETFL (get/set flags like O_NONBLOCK), F_GETFD/F_SETFD (get/set fd flags like FD_CLOEXEC), F_DUPFD/F_DUPFD_CLOEXEC (dup to >= arg).
acceptance_criteria_chirho: lseek moves file position correctly for all whence values
fcntl F_DUPFD duplicates to fd >= arg

implementation_tasks_chirho.title_chirho: Implement basic signal infrastructure (kill, SIGKILL, SIGSEGV)
implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Implement signal sending and delivery. kill(pid, sig): send signal to process. Signal pending set per task. On return from syscall or interrupt, check pending signals and deliver. SIGKILL: immediately terminate process (cannot be caught). SIGSEGV: terminate on segfault (triggered by page fault handler for user-space faults). Basic rt_sigaction for setting signal handlers (Phase 4 completes this).
acceptance_criteria_chirho: kill() sends signal to target process
SIGSEGV triggered on user page fault
Signals delivered on return to user space
Signal pending mask tracks undelivered signals

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Implement uname(buf). Fill struct utsname with: sysname='Linux' (for compatibility), nodename='lineluya', release='6.19.8-lineluya-chirho', version='#1 SMP', machine='x86_64', domainname='(none)'. Return 'Linux' as sysname so userspace (BusyBox, musl) detects a Linux kernel.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: uname() fills all fields of struct utsname

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Implement: getpid() returns current PID, getppid() returns parent PID, getuid/geteuid/getgid/getegid return 0 (root for now), access/faccessat (check file permissions), umask(mask) set/return file creation mask, sysinfo() fill struct sysinfo (uptime, loads, totalram, freeram, procs).

Implement: nanosleep/clock_nanosleep (sleep using timer), clock_gettime (CLOCK_REALTIME, CLOCK_MONOTONIC from TSC/PIT), gettimeofday, time, link/unlink/symlink/readlink/rename/chmod/chown, truncate/ftruncate, mknod (create device nodes), poll (basic I/O readiness), prlimit64 (get/set resource limits), getrlimit/setrlimit, getrandom (random bytes).
acceptance_criteria_chirho: nanosleep suspends task for specified duration
poll reports I/O readiness for fds

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Implement futex(uaddr, op, val, timeout, uaddr2, val3). Essential for userspace synchronization (mutexes, condition variables). FUTEX_WAIT: if *uaddr == val, block caller until FUTEX_WAKE. FUTEX_WAKE: wake up to val waiters blocked on uaddr. Use a global hash table of wait queues keyed by (mm, uaddr) pair. This is needed by musl/glibc for thread synchronization.

Implement set_robust_list(head, len) and get_robust_list(pid, head_ptr, len_ptr). Store robust futex list head in task struct. On task exit, kernel walks the robust list and performs FUTEX_WAKE on each entry. This is called early by glibc/musl init. Minimal implementation: just store the pointer, walk on exit.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: set_robust_list stores head pointer in task
On task exit, robust futexes are woken

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Load initramfs (cpio archive) from boot params or embedded in kernel. Parse cpio newc format: extract files, directories, symlinks, device nodes into root tmpfs. This provides the initial filesystem content including /bin/busybox, /etc/inittab, /init script. Support both compressed (gzip) and uncompressed cpio.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: Files extracted with correct content and permissions
Device nodes created with correct major/minor

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Create a minimal initramfs containing: statically linked BusyBox (musl), /init script that mounts /proc, /dev, /sys and runs /bin/sh, /etc/inittab, symlinks for common commands (ls, cat, echo, mkdir, etc.). Build as cpio.gz archive. Add build script to xtask. The init script should output a banner and drop to shell.

After extracting initramfs, kernel creates PID 1 process (init): fork from kernel idle task, execve('/init', ...). This is the first user process. If /init not found, try /sbin/init, /etc/init, /bin/init, /bin/sh. Implement the kernel_init_chirho function that does this handoff. After exec, kernel idle loop runs as PID 0.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: Init process has fds 0/1/2 pointing to console
Init process has root filesystem as cwd
BusyBox init starts and drops to shell
Shell prompt visible on serial console

implementation_tasks_chirho.title_chirho: QEMU integration test for Phase 3 (BusyBox shell)
implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Create automated test: boot kernel with BusyBox initramfs, wait for shell prompt, send commands via serial (echo hello, ls /, cat /proc/cpuinfo), verify expected output, test exit. Add as cargo xtask test-phase3.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: Test exits cleanly with pass/fail status

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Implement the dentry cache to avoid repeated path lookups hitting the filesystem. Cache mapping from (parent_dentry, name) -> dentry. LRU eviction of unused dentries. Negative dentries (cache ENOENT results). d_lookup_chirho() checks cache before filesystem. d_add_chirho() inserts into cache. d_drop_chirho() removes from cache. Hash table indexed by (parent, name hash).
acceptance_criteria_chirho: Repeated path lookups served from cache
Cache entries evicted under memory pressure
Negative dentries prevent repeated ENOENT lookups

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Implement basic sysfs: /sys/class/ (device classes), /sys/devices/ (device hierarchy), /sys/bus/ (bus types), /sys/block/ (block devices), /sys/kernel/ (kernel params like hostname), /sys/fs/ (filesystem info). Each sysfs file maps to a kernel object attribute. Implement show/store callbacks for reading/writing sysfs attributes.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: Sysfs attributes backed by kernel object callbacks

implementation_tasks_chirho.title_chirho: Implement personality syscall and prctl basics
implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: personality(persona): set execution domain (PER_LINUX default). prctl(option, ...): PR_SET_NAME (set task name/comm), PR_GET_NAME, PR_SET_DUMPABLE, PR_GET_DUMPABLE, PR_SET_PDEATHSIG (signal on parent death), PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS (for seccomp). These are called early by many programs.

poll(fds, nfds, timeout): check multiple fds for readiness (POLLIN, POLLOUT, POLLERR, POLLHUP). Block until at least one fd is ready or timeout expires. pselect6/select: similar but with fd_set bitmask interface. These are needed by many programs (BusyBox ash uses poll for input). Implement poll method on file operations for pipe, TTY, socket.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: POLLIN reported when data available for read
POLLHUP reported when pipe write-end closed

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: readlink(path, buf, bufsize): read value of symbolic link into buf. readlinkat(dirfd, path, buf, bufsize): same with dirfd. Return number of bytes placed in buf (not NUL-terminated). For symlinks stored inline in inode, copy from inode data. For symlinks with external blocks, read from storage.

Upgrade sys_write from Phase 2 (serial-only) to use the VFS. Look up FileChirho from fd table, call file_ops.write() with user buffer data. Handle partial writes (return bytes written). Update file position (f_pos). For non-seekable files (pipes, sockets), don't update position.

mknod(pathname, mode, dev): create special file (device node, FIFO, socket). Parse mode for file type: S_IFCHR (character device), S_IFBLK (block device), S_IFIFO (named pipe). For devices: store major/minor in dev parameter. For FIFO: create named pipe. Needed by devtmpfs and udev for creating /dev entries.

implementation_tasks_chirho.title_chirho: Implement sys_mount_chirho with filesystem type dispatch
implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Implement mount(source, target, filesystemtype, mountflags, data). Register filesystem types (tmpfs, procfs, sysfs, devtmpfs, ext4). On mount: look up filesystem type by name, call its mount/fill_super callback, create vfsmount structure at target path. Support flags: MS_RDONLY, MS_NOSUID, MS_NODEV, MS_NOEXEC, MS_REMOUNT, MS_BIND.

Implement rt_sigaction(sig, act, oldact, sigsetsize). Register custom signal handlers. struct sigaction contains: sa_handler (SIG_DFL, SIG_IGN, or user function pointer), sa_mask (signals to block during handler), sa_flags (SA_RESTART, SA_NOCLDSTOP, SA_SIGINFO, SA_ONSTACK, SA_RESETHAND, SA_NODEFER). Store sigaction array in task's signal struct. Cannot catch SIGKILL or SIGSTOP.

implementation_tasks_chirho.title_chirho: Implement signal delivery to user-space handler
implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: When delivering a signal with a custom handler: save current pt_regs onto user stack as signal frame (struct rt_sigframe containing ucontext_t, siginfo_t), set up user RIP to point to sa_handler, RDI=signum, RSI=&siginfo, RDX=&ucontext, set signal return trampoline address (SA_RESTORER or kernel-provided trampoline that calls rt_sigreturn). Block sa_mask signals during handler execution.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: Signal frame pushed onto user stack with saved registers
User RIP set to signal handler address
Handler receives correct signum, siginfo, ucontext args
Return address set to rt_sigreturn trampoline

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Implement rt_sigreturn(). Called when signal handler returns (via SA_RESTORER trampoline). Restore saved registers from signal frame on user stack (ucontext_t.uc_mcontext). Restore signal mask from uc_sigmask. Validate frame to prevent stack corruption attacks. Resume execution at the point where the signal interrupted.

rt_sigprocmask(how, set, oldset, sigsetsize): SIG_BLOCK adds signals to mask, SIG_UNBLOCK removes, SIG_SETMASK replaces. sigaltstack(ss, old_ss): set alternate signal stack for handler execution (SA_ONSTACK). Required by many programs for safe signal handling.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: Blocked signals stay pending until unblocked
sigaltstack sets alternate stack for signal delivery

implementation_tasks_chirho.title_chirho: Implement TTY subsystem core (line discipline, termios)
implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Implement the terminal subsystem. TTY struct with: input buffer (canonical line editing), output buffer, termios settings (c_iflag, c_oflag, c_cflag, c_lflag, c_cc), foreground process group, session. Line discipline: canonical mode (line buffering with editing: backspace, Ctrl-C, Ctrl-D, Ctrl-Z), raw mode (no processing). Implement TCGETS/TCSETS ioctls for termios. Connect serial UART to a TTY device.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: Canonical mode buffers input until newline
Backspace editing works in canonical mode
Ctrl-C sends SIGINT to foreground process group

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Implement pseudo-terminals for programs like SSH, screen, tmux. openat('/dev/ptmx') creates master PTY fd and allocates slave /dev/pts/N. Data written to master appears as input on slave and vice versa. ptsname/unlockpt/grantpt via ioctls (TIOCGPTN, TIOCSPTLCK). Slave PTY acts as a regular TTY (line discipline, termios). Mount devpts filesystem at /dev/pts.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: Data flows between master and slave

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Implement session and process group management. setsid(): create new session, caller becomes session leader. setpgid(pid, pgid): set process group. getpgrp/getpgid: get process group. tcsetpgrp/tcgetpgrp (via TIOCSPGRP/TIOCGPGRP ioctls): set/get foreground process group of TTY. Each session has a controlling terminal. Orphaned process group handling.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: Foreground process group receives TTY signals
Background process group stopped on TTY read (SIGTTIN)

implementation_tasks_chirho.title_chirho: Implement job control signals (SIGTSTP, SIGCONT, SIGTTIN, SIGTTOU)
implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Full job control: Ctrl-Z sends SIGTSTP to foreground group, stopping processes (state = TASK_STOPPED). SIGCONT resumes stopped processes. Background processes receive SIGTTIN when trying to read from TTY (stops them), SIGTTOU when writing to TTY (if TOSTOP termios flag set). Shell manages job control via waitpid(WUNTRACED|WCONTINUED).

Replace round-robin with EEVDF (Earliest Eligible Virtual Deadline First) scheduler, which replaced CFS in Linux 6.6. Each task has: virtual runtime (vruntime), virtual deadline, weight (from nice value). Tasks organized in red-black tree by virtual deadline. Pick task with earliest eligible virtual deadline. Time slice proportional to weight. Implement nice values (-20 to 19) and corresponding weights. Handle wakeup/sleep/preemption.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: Newly woken tasks get fair share of CPU
CPU-bound tasks do not starve I/O-bound tasks

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Extend procfs with per-process detail files: /proc/[pid]/maps (show VMAs with addresses, permissions, file mappings), /proc/[pid]/status (human-readable process info), /proc/[pid]/stat (machine-readable, 52+ fields matching Linux format), /proc/[pid]/statm (memory stats), /proc/[pid]/fd/ (directory of symlinks to open files), /proc/[pid]/cwd, /proc/[pid]/root, /proc/[pid]/exe symlinks.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: Symlinks for cwd, root, exe resolve correctly

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Implement clone3(cl_args, size) which supersedes clone() with a cleaner extensible struct interface (struct clone_args). Support flags: CLONE_VM, CLONE_FS, CLONE_FILES, CLONE_SIGHAND, CLONE_THREAD, CLONE_NEWPID, CLONE_PARENT_SETTID, CLONE_CHILD_SETTID, CLONE_CHILD_CLEARTID. Handle child stack setup. This is used by modern glibc for pthread_create.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: clone3 creates new process/thread with specified flags
CLONE_THREAD shares signal handlers and PID group
TID stored at parent_tidptr and child_tidptr

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Implement full credential (CredChirho) management. Syscalls: setuid, setgid, setreuid, setregid, setresuid, getresuid, setresgid, getresgid, setfsuid, setfsgid, setgroups, getgroups. CredChirho struct holds: uid, gid, euid, egid, suid, sgid, fsuid, fsgid, supplementary groups. Copy-on-write credentials (inherit on fork, copy on set).
acceptance_criteria_chirho: Only root (euid=0) can setuid to arbitrary user

implementation_tasks_chirho.title_chirho: QEMU integration test for Phase 4 (bash job control)
implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Test that bash or dash runs with job control. Send commands: start background job (sleep 100 &), Ctrl-Z to stop foreground job, fg to resume, jobs to list, kill to terminate. Verify signal delivery and terminal interaction work end-to-end.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: Shell starts with job control enabled

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Create WaitQueueChirho: a list of tasks waiting for an event. wait_event_chirho(wq, condition): put current task to sleep on wq until condition is true. wake_up_chirho(wq): wake one or all sleeping tasks. Used by: pipe read/write blocking, futex, socket blocking, sleep, signal delivery. Implement both exclusive and non-exclusive waits.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: Tasks sleep on wait queue until woken
Exclusive wait wakes only one task
Interruptible wait returns on pending signal

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: timerfd_create(clockid, flags): create timer file descriptor. timerfd_settime(fd, flags, new_value, old_value): arm/disarm timer. timerfd_gettime(fd, curr_value): get remaining time. When timer expires, fd becomes readable (returns u64 count of expirations). Support TFD_NONBLOCK, TFD_CLOEXEC. Used by systemd and event loops.

eventfd2(initval, flags): create event fd backed by u64 counter. write adds to counter, read returns and resets counter. EFD_SEMAPHORE flag: read returns 1 and decrements. signalfd4(fd, mask, flags): create fd that receives signals as siginfo_t structs. Both critical for modern event-driven programs (systemd, libev, libuv).
acceptance_criteria_chirho: signalfd delivers signals as readable data

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: inotify_init1(flags): create inotify instance fd. inotify_add_watch(fd, pathname, mask): watch path for events (IN_CREATE, IN_DELETE, IN_MODIFY, IN_MOVED_FROM, IN_MOVED_TO, IN_CLOSE_WRITE, etc.). inotify_rm_watch(fd, wd): remove watch. Reading fd returns inotify_event structs. Used by systemd-udevd and file managers.

Track per-process resource limits: RLIMIT_NOFILE (max open fds), RLIMIT_AS (max virtual memory), RLIMIT_STACK (max stack size), RLIMIT_CORE (core dump size), RLIMIT_NPROC (max processes), RLIMIT_CPU (CPU time), RLIMIT_FSIZE (max file size), etc. prlimit64(pid, resource, new_rlim, old_rlim). Enforce limits in relevant syscalls.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: RLIMIT_NOFILE limits max open file descriptors

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: memfd_create(name, flags): create anonymous file backed by memory, returns fd. Useful for sharing memory between processes via fd passing. Support MFD_CLOEXEC, MFD_ALLOW_SEALING. Implement ftruncate to resize. mmap the memfd for shared memory. Also implement /dev/shm as tmpfs mount for POSIX shared memory (shm_open).
acceptance_criteria_chirho: mmap maps the memfd for read/write
Multiple processes can mmap same memfd

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: madvise(addr, length, advice): hint to kernel about memory usage pattern. MADV_DONTNEED (free pages, will be zeroed on next access), MADV_WILLNEED (prefetch), MADV_FREE (lazy free). mremap(old_address, old_size, new_size, flags): grow or shrink an existing mapping. MREMAP_MAYMOVE allows relocation if can't grow in place. Needed by memory allocators (jemalloc, glibc malloc).
acceptance_criteria_chirho: MADV_DONTNEED frees pages (zeroed on next access)
mremap grows mappings in place if possible
Both return correct error codes for invalid arguments

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: kill(pid, sig): send signal to process or process group. If pid > 0, send to specific process. If pid == 0, send to all processes in caller's process group. If pid == -1, send to all processes. If pid < -1, send to process group |pid|. tgkill(tgid, tid, sig): send signal to specific thread. tkill(tid, sig): deprecated but still used. Permission check: sender must have CAP_KILL or same uid as target.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: kill sends signal to target process

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: rt_sigpending(set): return the set of signals that are pending for the calling thread (union of thread-pending and process-pending). rt_sigsuspend(mask): temporarily replace signal mask with given mask and suspend until a signal is delivered (then restore old mask). Both needed for full POSIX signal semantics.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: rt_sigsuspend atomically replaces mask and waits

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: waitid(idtype, id, infop, options, rusage): more flexible than wait4. idtype: P_PID (specific), P_PGID (process group), P_ALL (any child), P_PIDFD (pidfd). options: WEXITED, WSTOPPED, WCONTINUED, WNOHANG, WNOWAIT. Fills siginfo_t with detailed exit info. Needed by systemd.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: waitid waits for specified child type

implementation_tasks_chirho.title_chirho: Implement SIGCHLD delivery on child exit
implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: When a child process exits, send SIGCHLD to its parent. If parent has SA_NOCLDSTOP flag clear, also send SIGCHLD when child is stopped (SIGTSTP). If parent has SA_NOCLDWAIT, do not create zombie (auto-reap). Set si_code in siginfo_t: CLD_EXITED, CLD_KILLED, CLD_DUMPED, CLD_STOPPED, CLD_CONTINUED. This is how shells and init detect child exit.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: SIGCHLD sent to parent on child exit

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Create the block I/O abstraction layer. BioChirho struct: represents a block I/O request with sector number, length, data buffer, completion callback. RequestQueueChirho: manages pending I/O requests for a block device. BlockDeviceOpsChirho trait: submit_bio, capacity, sector_size. Support merging adjacent requests and I/O scheduling (simple FIFO initially).
acceptance_criteria_chirho: BioChirho struct encapsulates block I/O requests

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Implement VirtIO block device driver for QEMU. Discover VirtIO PCI devices (vendor 0x1AF4, device 0x1001 or transitional). Initialize virtqueues (descriptor table, available ring, used ring). Submit read/write requests via virtqueue. Handle completion interrupts. Register as block device with block I/O layer. Support QEMU's -drive format.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: VirtIO PCI device discovered and initialized
Block read requests return correct data

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Parse GPT (GUID Partition Table) from block device. Read protective MBR at LBA 0, GPT header at LBA 1, partition entry array starting at LBA 2. Validate CRC32 checksums. Extract partition entries: type GUID, unique GUID, start/end LBA, attributes, name. Create sub-devices for each partition (e.g., /dev/vda1, /dev/vda2). Also support legacy MBR parsing.

Implement the page cache for caching disk blocks in memory. AddressSpaceChirho per inode maps file page indices to physical pages. read_page_chirho(): check cache first, read from disk on miss. write_page_chirho(): write to cache, mark page dirty. Writeback: flush dirty pages to disk periodically or on sync. LRU eviction when memory pressure. This is critical for filesystem performance.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: sync forces dirty pages to disk

implementation_tasks_chirho.title_chirho: Implement ext4 superblock and group descriptor parsing
implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Read ext4 superblock from block device (offset 1024 bytes). Parse: magic (0xEF53), block size, inode count, block count, blocks per group, inodes per group, feature flags (FEATURE_INCOMPAT_EXTENTS, FEATURE_INCOMPAT_64BIT, etc.). Read group descriptor table. Validate filesystem integrity. Support 64-bit and 32-bit ext4 variants.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: Incompatible features cause mount failure with clear error

implementation_tasks_chirho.title_chirho: Implement ext4 inode reading and extent tree
implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Read ext4 inodes from inode table (computed from inode number, group, and inode table block). Parse inode struct: mode, uid, gid, size, timestamps, block pointers. For ext4 with extents (FEATURE_INCOMPAT_EXTENTS): parse extent tree header, index nodes, and leaf extents (ee_block, ee_start, ee_len) to map logical blocks to physical blocks. Support multi-level extent trees.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: Inodes read from correct disk location
Extent tree maps logical to physical blocks
Large files (> 4 extents) handled via tree traversal

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Read ext4 directories. Parse directory entries: inode number, record length, name length, file type, name. Support both linear directories (simple linked list of entries) and hash tree directories (HTree / dx_hash for large directories). Implement directory lookup (find entry by name) and directory iteration (getdents64).
acceptance_criteria_chirho: Directory lookup finds entries by name

implementation_tasks_chirho.title_chirho: Implement ext4 read-only mounting and file reading
implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Wire ext4 into VFS: implement SuperOpsChirho, InodeOpsChirho, FileOpsChirho for ext4. mount() creates ext4 superblock, reads root inode (inode 2). Path resolution walks ext4 directories. read() reads file data via extent tree and page cache. Support symlinks (inline and extent-based). Register ext4 filesystem type.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: ls / shows ext4 root directory contents

implementation_tasks_chirho.title_chirho: Implement ext4 write support (block allocation, inode update)
implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Enable ext4 writes: allocate blocks from block group bitmaps (multi-block allocator mballoc or simple bitmap allocator). Update inode on disk after metadata changes. Create new directory entries. Implement file write (allocate new extents, update inode size). Handle block deallocation on truncate/delete. Update group descriptor free counts.

Implement journaling for crash consistency. Journal is a circular log on a dedicated inode (inode 8). Transaction lifecycle: start -> add metadata blocks to transaction -> commit (write to journal) -> checkpoint (write to final location) -> clear from journal. Support ordered mode (default): data written before metadata commit. Implement journal recovery on mount (replay uncommitted transactions).
acceptance_criteria_chirho: Journal recovery replays on unclean mount
Checkpoint writes journal data to final location

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: fsync(fd): flush all data and metadata for file to disk. fdatasync(fd): flush data and only metadata needed to access data (not atime/mtime unless size changed). For ext4: commit journal transaction containing this file's blocks. For tmpfs: no-op. sync(): flush all dirty pages and journal for all filesystems. syncfs(fd): sync the filesystem containing fd.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: fsync persists file data and metadata to disk
fdatasync persists data and essential metadata
Data survives QEMU reset after fsync

implementation_tasks_chirho.title_chirho: QEMU integration test for Phase 5 (persistent storage)
implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Test: create ext4 disk image, boot kernel, mount ext4, create file, write data, fsync, reboot QEMU, verify file persists. Test both reads and writes, directory operations, symlinks on ext4.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: File created and written to ext4

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: statfs(path, buf) and fstatfs(fd, buf): return filesystem statistics. Fill struct statfs with: f_type (filesystem magic), f_bsize (block size), f_blocks (total blocks), f_bfree (free blocks), f_bavail (available blocks), f_files (total inodes), f_ffree (free inodes), f_namelen (max name length), f_frsize (fragment size). Each filesystem type provides its own statfs implementation.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: statfs returns correct block counts for ext4
df command shows correct filesystem info

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Implement setxattr, getxattr, listxattr, removexattr (and f/l variants). Extended attributes store name-value pairs on inodes. Namespaces: user.*, security.*, system.*, trusted.*. For ext4: store in inode body (if space) or separate xattr block. For tmpfs: store in hash table. Needed for security contexts (security.selinux) and capabilities (security.capability).

Implement zero-copy data transfer syscalls. sendfile(out_fd, in_fd, offset, count): copy between fds in kernel (no user-space bounce). splice(fd_in, off_in, fd_out, off_out, len, flags): move data between fd and pipe. copy_file_range(fd_in, off_in, fd_out, off_out, len, flags): server-side copy between files. These are critical for performance (used by web servers, cp, etc.).
acceptance_criteria_chirho: sendfile copies data between fds without user buffer
splice moves data between pipe and fd

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: readv(fd, iov, iovcnt): scatter-read into multiple buffers. writev(fd, iov, iovcnt): gather-write from multiple buffers. preadv/pwritev: same but with explicit file offset (no seek). preadv2/pwritev2: add flags parameter (RWF_HIPRI, RWF_DSYNC, RWF_SYNC, RWF_NOWAIT). Used heavily by databases and high-performance I/O.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: readv scatters data across multiple buffers
writev gathers data from multiple buffers
Atomic with respect to file position

implementation_tasks_chirho.title_chirho: Implement PCI BAR (Base Address Register) mapping
implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Read PCI BARs (Base Address Registers) to discover device MMIO and I/O port regions. Parse BAR type (memory vs I/O), 32-bit vs 64-bit, prefetchable flag. Map MMIO BARs into kernel virtual address space using page tables. Needed for VirtIO, AHCI, NVMe, and all PCI devices.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: MMIO BARs mapped to kernel virtual addresses
I/O port BARs accessible via in/out instructions

implementation_tasks_chirho.title_chirho: Implement VirtIO common initialization (PCI modern transport)
implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Implement VirtIO PCI modern transport (capability-based). Discover VirtIO PCI capabilities: common config, notify, ISR, device-specific, PCI config access. Initialize device: reset, set ACKNOWLEDGE, set DRIVER, negotiate features, set FEATURES_OK, configure virtqueues, set DRIVER_OK. Shared between virtio-blk, virtio-net, virtio-gpu, virtio-snd.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: VirtIO device discovered via PCI capabilities

implementation_tasks_chirho.title_chirho: Implement DMA and scatter-gather for block I/O
implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Implement DMA (Direct Memory Access) support for block device I/O. Create DMA-safe buffers: pages that are contiguous in physical memory and accessible by devices. Scatter-gather lists for multi-page I/O (list of [phys_addr, length] pairs). DMA address mapping (1:1 or via IOMMU). Bounce buffers for devices that can only access low memory. Needed by VirtIO and real hardware drivers.

Create the socket abstraction: SocketChirho struct (AF_INET, AF_INET6, AF_UNIX, AF_NETLINK), SockChirho trait with protocol-specific operations (connect, bind, listen, accept, sendmsg, recvmsg, poll). Socket integrates with VFS via file descriptor (socket creates an anonymous inode with socket file_operations). SockAddrChirho types for each address family.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: AF_INET, AF_INET6, AF_UNIX address families defined
Socket operations dispatched to protocol handler

implementation_tasks_chirho.title_chirho: Implement network device abstraction and loopback
implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Create NetDeviceChirho trait: transmit(skb), receive callback, get_stats, set_mtu. Implement SkBuffChirho (socket buffer) for packet data with head/data/tail/end pointers, push/pull operations for header manipulation. Implement loopback device (lo): transmit immediately delivers to receive path. Set up 127.0.0.1/8 on lo.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: Loopback device delivers packets to self

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Implement VirtIO network device driver. Initialize two virtqueues (receive and transmit). Post receive buffers. On packet receive: interrupt handler dequeues from used ring, wraps in SkBuffChirho, delivers to network stack. On transmit: add SkBuffChirho data to transmit virtqueue, notify device. Handle VirtIO-net header (flags, GSO type, header length, checksum).
acceptance_criteria_chirho: MAC address read from device config

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Ethernet frame handling: parse incoming frames (dst MAC, src MAC, EtherType), dispatch to protocol handler (0x0800=IPv4, 0x0806=ARP, 0x86DD=IPv6). Build outgoing frames with correct headers. ARP protocol: ARP table (IP -> MAC mapping), ARP request/reply handling, ARP cache with timeout, gratuitous ARP. Resolve neighbor MAC addresses before IP transmission.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: Ethernet frames parsed and dispatched by EtherType
ARP requests sent for unknown MAC addresses
ARP cache entries expire after timeout
Outgoing frames have correct Ethernet headers

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: IPv4 packet handling: parse IP header (version, IHL, total length, TTL, protocol, checksum, src/dst addr). Validate checksum. Dispatch to protocol handler (6=TCP, 17=UDP, 1=ICMP). Build outgoing IP packets with correct headers and checksum. Implement basic routing table (destination network -> gateway + interface). Support IP fragmentation for large packets. Decrement TTL and drop expired packets.

Implement ICMP protocol: respond to Echo Request (type 8) with Echo Reply (type 0). Send ICMP Destination Unreachable for unroutable packets. Support ping from userspace (raw socket or special handling). Checksum computation for ICMP packets. This enables basic network connectivity testing.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: Kernel responds to ICMP echo requests
ping from QEMU host to guest works
Destination Unreachable sent for unroutable packets

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Implement UDP protocol: parse UDP header (src port, dst port, length, checksum). Socket binding to port. Demultiplex incoming packets to bound sockets. sendto/recvfrom for sending/receiving datagrams. Per-socket receive buffer with configurable size. Support SO_REUSEADDR, SO_REUSEPORT. UDP checksum computation (pseudo-header included).
acceptance_criteria_chirho: UDP packets received and dispatched to socket

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Implement the full TCP state machine: CLOSED, LISTEN, SYN_SENT, SYN_RECEIVED, ESTABLISHED, FIN_WAIT_1, FIN_WAIT_2, CLOSE_WAIT, CLOSING, LAST_ACK, TIME_WAIT. Three-way handshake (SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK). Connection teardown (FIN, FIN-ACK). Handle RST. Sequence number management (ISN generation, wraparound). Per-connection transmit and receive buffers.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: Data transfer works in ESTABLISHED state

implementation_tasks_chirho.title_chirho: Implement TCP sliding window and congestion control
implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Implement TCP reliability: sliding window (advertised window, receive window), acknowledgment handling (cumulative ACKs), retransmission timer (RTO calculation with Karn's algorithm), fast retransmit (3 duplicate ACKs). Congestion control: slow start, congestion avoidance (AIMD), fast recovery. Nagle's algorithm (TCP_NODELAY to disable). Window scaling option (RFC 7323).
acceptance_criteria_chirho: Sliding window correctly limits outstanding data
Slow start and congestion avoidance work
Window scaling negotiated for large windows

implementation_tasks_chirho.title_chirho: Implement socket syscalls (bind, listen, accept, connect, send, recv)
implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Implement all socket-related syscalls: socket(), bind(), listen(), accept()/accept4(), connect(), sendto(), recvfrom(), sendmsg(), recvmsg(), shutdown(), setsockopt(), getsockopt(), getpeername(), getsockname(), socketpair(). Each dispatches to the protocol-specific implementation. Handle blocking/non-blocking modes, timeouts (SO_RCVTIMEO, SO_SNDTIMEO).
acceptance_criteria_chirho: TCP client can connect to external server

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Implement epoll for scalable I/O multiplexing. epoll_create1(flags): create epoll instance (backed by red-black tree of monitored fds). epoll_ctl(epfd, op, fd, event): EPOLL_CTL_ADD/MOD/DEL to manage watched fds. epoll_wait(epfd, events, maxevents, timeout): block until events ready or timeout. Support EPOLLIN, EPOLLOUT, EPOLLERR, EPOLLHUP, EPOLLET (edge-triggered), EPOLLONESHOT.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: Scales to thousands of fds efficiently

implementation_tasks_chirho.title_chirho: QEMU integration test for Phase 6 (network connectivity)
implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Test: configure QEMU user-mode networking, boot kernel, configure IP address, ping gateway, make TCP connection (wget a test file from host HTTP server), verify data integrity. Test DNS resolution if possible.

Implement Unix domain sockets (AF_UNIX). Support SOCK_STREAM (connection-oriented) and SOCK_DGRAM (datagram). Socket address is pathname or abstract (\0 prefix). Implement: bind to path (creates socket file), connect, listen/accept, send/recv. Support SCM_RIGHTS (fd passing between processes via sendmsg/recvmsg with cmsg) and SCM_CREDENTIALS (pid, uid, gid passing). Used by systemd, dbus, X11, Wayland.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: SCM_RIGHTS passes file descriptors between processes
