implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Implement Netlink sockets (AF_NETLINK) for kernel-userspace communication. NETLINK_ROUTE: routing and link management (ip addr, ip route, ip link). Parse and respond to RTM_GETLINK, RTM_NEWADDR, RTM_GETADDR, RTM_GETROUTE messages. Support multicast groups for event notification. Used by iproute2, udevd, NetworkManager, systemd-networkd.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: ip addr / ip route commands work

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Implement IP address assignment to interfaces, routing table management (add/delete routes, default gateway), and basic network interface configuration (up/down, MTU). Support DHCP client capability (by sending/receiving raw UDP packets). Configure DNS resolver via /etc/resolv.conf reading. Implement getaddrinfo-supporting infrastructure.

Implement basic IPv6: parse IPv6 header (next header chain), ICMPv6 (neighbor discovery, router solicitation), link-local address generation (fe80::/10 from MAC), global address assignment. Support dual-stack sockets (IPV6_V6ONLY option). Enough for basic IPv6 connectivity but not full feature parity with IPv4.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: Dual-stack sockets accept IPv4 and IPv6

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Implement TCP and UDP checksum computation. Pseudo-header checksum (src IP, dst IP, protocol, TCP length) combined with TCP header and data checksum. Implement both for outgoing packets (compute) and incoming (verify). Support checksum offloading flag for VirtIO-net. Optimize with 32-bit accumulator folded to 16-bit ones-complement.

implementation_tasks_chirho.title_chirho: Implement TCP listen backlog and accept queue
implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Implement TCP passive open (server side). listen(fd, backlog): set socket to LISTEN state, create SYN queue (incomplete connections) and accept queue (completed 3-way handshake). On incoming SYN: create request socket, send SYN-ACK, add to SYN queue. On incoming ACK (completing handshake): move to accept queue. accept(): dequeue from accept queue and return new connected socket. Handle SYN flood protection (SYN cookies optional).

implementation_tasks_chirho.title_chirho: Implement TCP keepalive and socket options
implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Implement TCP keepalive: periodic probes on idle connections (SO_KEEPALIVE, TCP_KEEPIDLE, TCP_KEEPINTVL, TCP_KEEPCNT). Additional socket options: TCP_NODELAY (disable Nagle), SO_RCVBUF/SO_SNDBUF (buffer sizes), SO_LINGER (close behavior), SO_REUSEADDR/SO_REUSEPORT, TCP_QUICKACK, TCP_CORK. These are required by most network applications.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: TCP keepalive probes sent on idle connections

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Implement capabilities (CAP_SYS_ADMIN, CAP_NET_ADMIN, CAP_NET_RAW, CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE, etc., ~41 capabilities). Three sets per task: permitted, effective, inheritable. capget/capset syscalls. Check capabilities instead of just uid==0 for privileged operations. Capability bounding set. File capabilities via extended attributes. Implement cap_capable() check throughout kernel.

Implement PID namespace: processes in child namespace see different PID space (PID 1 is the namespace init). Implement unshare(CLONE_NEWPID) and clone with CLONE_NEWPID. PID translation between namespaces. /proc shows PIDs relative to the reader's namespace. Namespace init (PID 1) reaps orphans within namespace. Killing namespace init kills all processes in namespace.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: New PID namespace created via clone/unshare
Processes see PIDs relative to their namespace
PID 1 in namespace acts as init

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Implement mount namespace: each namespace has its own mount tree. unshare(CLONE_NEWNS) copies current mount tree. Changes in one namespace not visible in others. pivot_root() changes root filesystem within namespace. Needed for container filesystem isolation.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: New mount namespace copies mount tree
Mounts in child namespace invisible to parent

implementation_tasks_chirho.title_chirho: Implement network, UTS, IPC, user, cgroup namespaces
implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Implement remaining namespaces: Network (CLONE_NEWNET): isolated network stack, interfaces, routing, firewall rules. UTS (CLONE_NEWUTS): isolated hostname/domainname. IPC (CLONE_NEWIPC): isolated SysV IPC and POSIX mqueues. User (CLONE_NEWUSER): UID/GID mapping, unprivileged namespace creation. Cgroup (CLONE_NEWCGROUP): isolated cgroup root. setns() to enter existing namespace.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: User namespace allows unprivileged container creation

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Implement cgroups v2 unified hierarchy. cgroupfs mounted at /sys/fs/cgroup. Controllers: cpu (cpu.max, cpu.weight), memory (memory.max, memory.current, memory.swap.max, OOM), io (io.max, io.weight), pids (pids.max). Processes assigned to cgroups via cgroup.procs file. Subtree control via cgroup.subtree_control. Resource accounting and enforcement.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: PIDs controller limits number of processes

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Implement seccomp (secure computing). seccomp(SECCOMP_SET_MODE_FILTER) installs a BPF filter that examines each syscall. BPF program can return: SECCOMP_RET_ALLOW, SECCOMP_RET_KILL, SECCOMP_RET_ERRNO, SECCOMP_RET_TRACE, SECCOMP_RET_LOG. Implement classic BPF interpreter for the filter programs. Filters inherited across fork/exec. prctl(PR_SET_SECCOMP) also supported. Essential for container security.

implementation_tasks_chirho.title_chirho: QEMU integration test for Phase 7 (Docker hello-world)
implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Test: install minimal container runtime (runc or contained), create OCI bundle with hello-world image, run container with PID/mount/network namespaces and cgroups. Verify container sees isolated PID 1, isolated filesystem, resource limits enforced. This is the Docker hello-world equivalent.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: Container runs with isolated PID namespace
Container filesystem isolated via mount namespace

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Implement overlay filesystem for container image layering. overlayfs mounts a union of upper (writable) and lower (read-only) directories. Reads check upper first then lower. Writes go to upper (copy-up from lower if needed). Whiteout files (.wh.) mark deletions. Opaque directories. Multiple lower layers. This is how Docker/containerd layer images.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: Lower layer files visible in merged view
Writes create files in upper layer
Copy-up works for modified lower files
Whiteout files hide lower layer entries

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: chroot(path): change root directory for current process. pivot_root(new_root, put_old): atomically swap root filesystem (new_root becomes /, old root moved to put_old). pivot_root is more secure than chroot (moves old root out of view). Used by container runtimes to switch to container rootfs. Validate that new_root is a mount point.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: Old root accessible at put_old after pivot

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: unshare(flags): create new namespaces for calling process. setns(fd, nstype): enter an existing namespace via /proc/[pid]/ns/* file descriptor. Support all namespace types: CLONE_NEWPID, CLONE_NEWNS, CLONE_NEWNET, CLONE_NEWUTS, CLONE_NEWIPC, CLONE_NEWUSER, CLONE_NEWCGROUP. Implement /proc/[pid]/ns/* as symlinks showing namespace inode numbers.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: setns enters existing namespace from fd
Container runtime can set up namespaces

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Implement Linux Security Module (LSM) hook framework. Define security hooks at key decision points: file open, mmap, socket create, task create, capability check, etc. Each hook calls registered security module callbacks. Implement a basic 'capability' LSM (default). Framework allows future addition of AppArmor/SELinux-like modules. Hook list is static (no runtime registration/removal).
acceptance_criteria_chirho: Security hooks called at decision points
Hook framework extensible for new modules

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Create /proc/[pid]/ns/ directory with symlinks for each namespace: pid, mnt, net, uts, ipc, user, cgroup. Each symlink target format: 'nstype:[inode_number]'. Opening these files returns a fd that can be passed to setns(). Comparing inode numbers tells if two processes share a namespace.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: Symlink targets show namespace type and inode
Opening ns file returns fd for setns
Different namespaces have different inode numbers

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Implement cpu cgroup controller for resource limiting. Files: cpu.max (bandwidth limit in 'quota period' format, e.g., '200000 100000' = 200ms per 100ms), cpu.weight (1-10000, proportional sharing), cpu.stat (usage_usec, user_usec, system_usec, nr_periods, nr_throttled, throttled_usec). Enforce bandwidth limiting in scheduler: track per-cgroup CPU usage, throttle when quota exceeded, refill each period.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: Throttled processes unthrottled at period boundary

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Implement memory cgroup controller. Files: memory.max (hard limit, triggers OOM), memory.high (soft limit, triggers reclaim), memory.current (current usage), memory.min/memory.low (protection from reclaim), memory.swap.max (swap limit), memory.stat (detailed stats). Track per-cgroup page ownership. On allocation: charge to cgroup. On free: uncharge. memory.max exceeded triggers cgroup OOM killer.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: memory.max triggers OOM on excess allocation

implementation_tasks_chirho.title_chirho: Implement Linux boot protocol bzImage format
implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Create a build pipeline that produces a Linux-compatible bzImage. Structure: 512-byte boot sector with boot_flag=0xAA55, setup sectors with setup_header (magic 'HdrS', protocol 2.15, loadflags, code32_start), then compressed kernel payload. The setup_header must be at correct offsets. Use objcopy and custom linker script to produce the format. GRUB2 should recognize and load this binary.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: GRUB2 recognizes and loads the binary
file command identifies it as Linux kernel

implementation_tasks_chirho.title_chirho: Implement struct boot_params / zero page parsing
implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Parse the zero page (struct boot_params) passed by bootloader in ESI register. Extract: E820 memory map (e820_entries count + e820_table array), command line (cmd_line_ptr), initrd location (ramdisk_image + ramdisk_size), screen info, ACPI RSDP address, EFI info. Use this instead of multiboot info for memory map and boot parameters.

Replace the legacy 8259 PIC with Local APIC + IOAPIC. Detect APIC via CPUID. Map Local APIC MMIO registers. Initialize: set spurious interrupt vector, enable APIC, configure timer (periodic or one-shot mode). IOAPIC: parse MADT (ACPI) for IOAPIC address and ISA interrupt redirections. Program IOAPIC redirection entries for keyboard, serial, etc. Handle APIC timer for preemption on each CPU.

Enable multi-processor boot. Parse MADT (ACPI) to find all CPUs (Local APIC IDs). BSP (bootstrap processor) sends INIT-SIPI-SIPI sequence to wake APs (application processors). APs execute trampoline code (real mode -> protected mode -> long mode), then enter Rust code. Each AP sets up its own GDT, IDT, per-CPU data, kernel stack. Per-CPU run queues for scheduler. Implement spinlocks for cross-CPU synchronization.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: APs enter long mode and execute Rust code

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Parse ACPI tables for hardware discovery. Find RSDP (Root System Description Pointer) from boot_params or scan memory. Parse RSDT/XSDT to find table pointers. Parse key tables: MADT (APIC info, CPU count), FADT (power management), HPET (timers), MCFG (PCIe configuration). Validate checksums. Create Rust structs for each table type.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: MADT parsed for CPU and IOAPIC info

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Parse kernel command line string (from boot_params.cmd_line_ptr). Support key=value and boolean parameters. Essential parameters: root= (root device), init= (init program path), console= (console device, e.g., ttyS0,115200), quiet, debug, loglevel=, panic=. Make parameters accessible via a global config struct.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: Command line parsed into key-value pairs
init= parameter overrides default init path

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Enumerate PCI devices using configuration space access (I/O ports 0xCF8/0xCFC for legacy, MMIO via MCFG for PCIe). Scan all buses/devices/functions. Read vendor ID, device ID, class code, BARs, interrupt info. Build device tree. Support MSI/MSI-X interrupt allocation. This is required for real hardware device discovery.

AHCI driver: PCI class 01:06, initialize ABAR MMIO, set up command lists and FIS receive areas per port, send IDENTIFY DEVICE, implement read/write DMA commands. NVMe driver: PCI class 01:08:02, initialize admin queue, create I/O submission/completion queues, send Identify commands, implement read/write via NVMe commands. Register both as block devices.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: Read/write operations work on real hardware

implementation_tasks_chirho.title_chirho: Boot on real x86_64 hardware via GRUB2
implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Integration test on real hardware: install Lineluya bzImage on a USB drive or disk partition, configure GRUB2 with 'linux /boot/lineluya-chirho' entry, boot on a real x86_64 machine. Kernel should boot, parse ACPI, initialize APIC, detect and start all CPUs, find storage device, mount root filesystem, run init.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: Kernel boots to serial console output

implementation_tasks_chirho.title_chirho: Implement real-mode to long-mode boot stub
implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Write the startup assembly that runs when GRUB2 transfers control. Sequence: receive boot_params pointer in ESI, set up minimal page tables (identity-map first 4GB), enable PAE (CR4.PAE), set LME in EFER MSR, load CR3, enable paging (CR0.PG), jump to 64-bit code segment. The 64-bit code then sets up full kernel page tables and calls the Rust kernel_main.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: Real mode code sets up identity-mapped page tables
Rust kernel_main called with correct environment

implementation_tasks_chirho.title_chirho: Implement early console (earlycon) for boot debugging
implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Implement early console output before full driver initialization. Parse console= kernel command line parameter. Support: serial UART (ttyS0, configurable baud), VGA text mode (if available). Output boot messages as early as possible. Later transition to full TTY-backed console. This is critical for debugging boot failures on real hardware.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: Boot messages visible from earliest kernel code
Works on both QEMU and real hardware
Graceful transition to full console driver

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Implement high-resolution timekeeping. TSC (Time Stamp Counter): calibrate frequency against PIT or HPET, use RDTSC for nanosecond-resolution time. HPET (High Precision Event Timer): parse ACPI HPET table, map MMIO registers, use as reference clock and event timer. Implement clocksource abstraction with TSC as preferred source. APIC timer calibration against HPET/PIT.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: HPET used as reference if TSC unreliable

implementation_tasks_chirho.title_chirho: Implement UEFI stub for direct UEFI boot
implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Add EFI handover protocol support to the bzImage. UEFI firmware or bootloader can call the handover entry point directly. Parse EFI system table, use UEFI boot services for memory map (before ExitBootServices), framebuffer, and runtime services. Handle the transition from UEFI environment to kernel's own page tables and data structures.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: EFI handover entry point in bzImage header
UEFI boot services used for memory map
Kernel boots via systemd-boot on UEFI system
UEFI runtime services accessible after boot

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Implement IPIs (Inter-Processor Interrupts) for SMP coordination. Use Local APIC ICR (Interrupt Command Register) to send IPIs. Implement: TLB shootdown IPI (flush TLB on remote CPUs after page table change), reschedule IPI (wake up remote CPU's scheduler), stop IPI (halt remote CPU on panic), function-call IPI (execute function on remote CPU).
acceptance_criteria_chirho: TLB shootdown IPI flushes remote CPU TLBs
Stop IPI halts remote CPUs on panic
IPI delivery reliable between all CPUs

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Implement per-CPU variable infrastructure. Each CPU gets its own copy of per-CPU data. Access current CPU's copy via GS segment offset. Define PerCpuVarChirho<T> with get/set that automatically selects current CPU's copy. Used for: current task pointer, run queue, statistics counters, preemption count. Must disable preemption while accessing per-CPU data.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: Each CPU has independent copy of per-CPU vars

implementation_tasks_chirho.title_chirho: Implement real NIC driver (Intel e1000e or Realtek)
implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Implement driver for a common real network interface card. Intel e1000e: PCI device 8086:10D3 or similar. Initialize: map MMIO, configure transmit/receive descriptor rings, set MAC address, enable interrupts. Transmit: place packet in TX descriptor ring, signal device. Receive: poll RX descriptor ring on interrupt, wrap in SkBuff. Link detection and auto-negotiation. Alternatively, implement Realtek 8169.

implementation_tasks_chirho.title_chirho: Implement complete x86_64 syscall table (~384 syscalls)
implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Fill in all remaining x86_64 syscalls from the syscall_64.tbl. Group into batches: remaining file operations, extended attributes (xattr), memory management (mremap, madvise, mlock, mincore), scheduling (sched_setattr/getattr), timers, extended socket options, extended process management (waitid, process_vm_readv/writev), miscellaneous. Stub unimplemented ones with -ENOSYS and track coverage.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: All ~384 common+64bit syscalls have entries in table
LTP syscall tests pass at >90% rate

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Implement io_uring for high-performance async I/O. io_uring_setup: create submission queue (SQ) and completion queue (CQ) as shared memory rings between kernel and user. io_uring_enter: submit SQEs and/or wait for CQEs. Support operations: IORING_OP_READV, IORING_OP_WRITEV, IORING_OP_FSYNC, IORING_OP_POLL_ADD, IORING_OP_ACCEPT, IORING_OP_CONNECT, IORING_OP_OPENAT. io_uring_register for buffer registration.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: SQ/CQ rings created in shared memory
Multiple ops supported (read, write, accept, connect)

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Implement the eBPF VM: 64-bit register set (r0-r10), instruction set (ALU, JMP, MEM, CALL), verifier (DAG analysis, bounds checking, type tracking), JIT compiler (optional, interpret first). Support BPF maps (hash, array, per-CPU). Hook points: kprobes, tracepoints, XDP, socket filters, cgroup hooks. bpf() syscall with BPF_PROG_LOAD, BPF_MAP_CREATE, BPF_MAP_LOOKUP_ELEM, etc.

Extend /proc with all entries needed by common tools: /proc/sys/ (sysctl interface), /proc/net/ (network statistics: tcp, udp, raw, unix, if_inet6), /proc/pressure/ (PSI), /proc/diskstats, /proc/vmstat, /proc/slabinfo, /proc/modules, /proc/interrupts, /proc/softirqs, /proc/buddyinfo, /proc/zoneinfo. Extend /sys with device model, block device info, kernel parameters.

Implement basic DRM (Direct Rendering Manager) and KMS (Kernel Mode Setting) framework. VirtIO-GPU driver for QEMU. Support: mode setting (resolution, refresh rate), framebuffer creation, dumb buffer allocation, page flipping. Expose /dev/dri/card0. Enough for a basic Wayland compositor or fbdev console.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: Basic Wayland client can display window

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Implement USB host controller driver for XHCI (USB 3.x). PCI device discovery, MMIO register mapping, command/event/transfer ring setup, device slot allocation, endpoint configuration. Support USB mass storage (bulk transfers), USB HID (interrupt transfers for keyboard/mouse). Device enumeration and descriptor parsing.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: USB mass storage devices accessible as block devices
USB hub support for multi-device setups

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Implement basic sound subsystem compatible with ALSA userspace. Create /dev/snd/ devices (pcmC0D0p for playback, controlC0 for mixer). Implement VirtIO-sound driver for QEMU testing. Support PCM playback (open, hw_params, prepare, write, start/stop). Implement ioctl-based ALSA API subset (SNDRV_PCM_IOCTL_HW_PARAMS, etc.).

Implement loadable kernel module support. Module binary format (Rust dylib or custom format). Module loading: parse module, relocate symbols, resolve kernel symbol dependencies, call module_init. Module unloading: call module_exit, free memory. Module parameters. /proc/modules listing. C ABI bridge layer for loading existing Linux .ko modules (stretch goal).

implementation_tasks_chirho.title_chirho: Implement System V IPC and POSIX message queues
implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: SysV IPC: shmget/shmat/shmdt/shmctl (shared memory), semget/semop/semctl (semaphores), msgget/msgsnd/msgrcv/msgctl (message queues). POSIX mqueues: mq_open, mq_send, mq_receive, mq_close, mq_unlink (via mqueue filesystem). eventfd and signalfd for modern IPC patterns.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: SysV shared memory works between processes

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Build a small ELF shared object (vDSO) that is mapped into every user process at a fixed address (AT_SYSINFO_EHDR in auxv). Contains user-accessible implementations of: clock_gettime, gettimeofday, time, getcpu. These read kernel-maintained data pages (vsyscall page) without a full syscall transition. Critical for performance as clock_gettime is called millions of times.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: vDSO ELF mapped into every process
vDSO data page updated by kernel on tick

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Final integration test: create a disk image with Alpine Linux rootfs (apk-based), boot Lineluya with this rootfs, verify: init system starts (OpenRC), login prompt appears, user can log in, apk package manager works, basic services start, networking works. This validates full Linux compatibility.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: Alpine Linux boots to login prompt
No kernel panics during normal operation

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Implement packet filtering framework. Netfilter hooks at: PREROUTING, INPUT, FORWARD, OUTPUT, POSTROUTING. nftables: userspace tool creates rules via AF_NETLINK. Rule evaluation engine (match/action chains). Support: accept, drop, reject, SNAT, DNAT, masquerade. Connection tracking (conntrack) for stateful filtering. Enough for basic firewall and NAT.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: Netfilter hooks called at packet processing points

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Implement kernel tracing infrastructure. tracefs mounted at /sys/kernel/tracing. Tracepoints at key locations (syscall entry/exit, scheduler events, interrupt entry/exit, memory allocation). Function tracer: instrument function entries/exits. Trace buffer: per-CPU ring buffer for trace events. trace_pipe for live event streaming. Available events in available_events file.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: Events stored in per-CPU ring buffer

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Implement POSIX interval timers: timer_create, timer_settime, timer_gettime, timer_delete. Support CLOCK_REALTIME, CLOCK_MONOTONIC, CLOCK_PROCESS_CPUTIME_ID, CLOCK_THREAD_CPUTIME_ID. Timer expiration delivers signal (SIGALRM or custom). Implement alarm() as wrapper. Per-process CPU time accounting for ITIMER_PROF and ITIMER_VIRTUAL. setitimer/getitimer for BSD compatibility.

Implement input subsystem for keyboard/mouse/touch events. Input device abstraction (InputDeviceChirho). Event types: EV_KEY (key press/release), EV_REL (mouse movement), EV_ABS (touch position). Create /dev/input/event* device nodes. evdev interface: read returns input_event structs (type, code, value, time). PS/2 keyboard driver as first input device. Used by Wayland, X11, libinput.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: Key events readable as input_event structs
libinput or evtest can read events

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Implement perf_event_open syscall for performance monitoring. Hardware counters via PMU (Performance Monitoring Unit): CPU cycles, instructions retired, cache misses, branch mispredictions. Software counters: context switches, page faults, CPU migrations. Per-task or system-wide monitoring. Sampling: generate interrupt on counter overflow, record sample (IP, stack trace). Read counters via read() on perf fd.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: Hardware PMU counters read via perf fd

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Implement basic power management via ACPI. Parse FADT for PM1a/PM1b control registers. Implement sys_reboot syscall with: LINUX_REBOOT_CMD_POWER_OFF (ACPI S5), LINUX_REBOOT_CMD_RESTART (keyboard controller reset or ACPI reset register), LINUX_REBOOT_CMD_HALT. Handle shutdown sequence: kill all processes, sync filesystems, unmount, then ACPI power off.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: poweroff command shuts down system via ACPI
All processes terminated before power off
Works on QEMU and real hardware

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Implement OOM killer that selects and kills processes when memory is exhausted. OOM score per process based on: resident memory size, oom_score_adj (/proc/[pid]/oom_score_adj, range -1000 to 1000), -1000 = never kill. On OOM: select highest-scored process, send SIGKILL, free its memory. Log OOM events. Support cgroup-scoped OOM (kill within cgroup). Trigger on: page allocation failure after reclaim attempts.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: OOM killer triggered on memory exhaustion

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Extend ELF loader to support dynamically linked binaries. When PT_INTERP segment present: load the dynamic linker (ld-linux-x86-64.so.2) as well. Map both the application and the interpreter. Set entry point to interpreter's entry (which will then load shared libraries and jump to application). Provide correct AT_BASE (interpreter load address) in auxv. Needed for glibc-linked binaries.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: Dynamic ELF with PT_INTERP loads both binary and interpreter
AT_BASE in auxv points to interpreter

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Implement rseq(rseq_ptr, rseq_len, flags, sig). Restartable sequences allow user-space per-CPU operations without syscalls. Register a rseq struct in user memory that kernel updates with current CPU number. On preemption or signal during critical section, kernel restarts the sequence. Needed by modern glibc (2.35+) which calls rseq early in initialization.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: CPU number updated on context switch

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: close_range(first, last, flags): close all fds in range [first, last]. CLOSE_RANGE_UNSHARE: unshare fd table first. CLOSE_RANGE_CLOEXEC: set CLOEXEC instead of closing. pidfd_open(pid, flags): open a process file descriptor for specified PID. pidfd usable with poll (becomes readable when process exits), waitid(P_PIDFD), pidfd_send_signal. Modern process management API used by systemd.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: CLOSE_RANGE_CLOEXEC sets flag instead of closing

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: statx(dirfd, pathname, flags, mask, statxbuf): extended stat with selective field retrieval. struct statx adds: creation time (btime), mount ID, file attributes (STATX_ATTR_COMPRESSED, STATX_ATTR_IMMUTABLE, etc.), stx_mnt_id. mask parameter selects which fields to populate (STATX_TYPE, STATX_MODE, STATX_SIZE, STATX_BTIME, etc.). Supports AT_STATX_SYNC_AS_STAT, AT_STATX_FORCE_SYNC, AT_STATX_DONT_SYNC.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: Selective field population via mask works

implementation_tasks_chirho.title_chirho: Implement mount_setattr, fsopen, fsconfig, fsmount syscalls
implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: New mount API (Linux 5.2+): fsopen(fs_name, flags) opens filesystem context. fsconfig(fd, cmd, key, value, aux) configures it (set source, options). fsmount(fd, flags, ms_flags) creates a mount. move_mount(from_dirfd, from_path, to_dirfd, to_path, flags) attaches it. mount_setattr(dirfd, path, flags, attr, size) changes mount attributes (read-only, nosuid, noexec). Used by systemd and modern containers.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: Compatible with systemd mount unit files

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: sched_setattr(pid, attr, flags): set scheduling policy and parameters. Support SCHED_NORMAL (SCHED_OTHER), SCHED_FIFO, SCHED_RR, SCHED_BATCH, SCHED_IDLE, SCHED_DEADLINE. struct sched_attr contains: sched_policy, sched_nice, sched_priority, sched_runtime/deadline/period (for SCHED_DEADLINE). sched_getattr returns current settings. Also implement sched_setaffinity/sched_getaffinity for CPU pinning.

Implement /proc/sys/ as a writable procfs tree for kernel tuning. Key entries: /proc/sys/kernel/hostname, /proc/sys/kernel/osrelease, /proc/sys/kernel/pid_max, /proc/sys/vm/overcommit_memory, /proc/sys/vm/swappiness, /proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_forward, /proc/sys/net/core/somaxconn, /proc/sys/fs/file-max, /proc/sys/fs/pipe-max-size. Reading returns current value, writing changes it.

Implement kernel log ring buffer (printk equivalent). All kernel log messages stored in a circular buffer. syslog(type, bufp, len) syscall: SYSLOG_ACTION_READ reads messages, SYSLOG_ACTION_READ_ALL reads all, SYSLOG_ACTION_SIZE_BUFFER returns buffer size, SYSLOG_ACTION_CLEAR clears. /dev/kmsg device for reading/writing kernel messages. Log levels (KERN_EMERG..KERN_DEBUG). dmesg command works.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: Kernel messages stored in ring buffer

implementation_tasks_chirho.title_chirho: Implement getdents64 with proper d_off handling
implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Ensure getdents64 returns correctly formatted linux_dirent64 entries with proper d_off values. d_off must be the offset to seek to for the next entry (not the current entry offset). d_reclen must be 8-byte aligned. d_type must correctly identify file type (DT_REG, DT_DIR, DT_LNK, DT_CHR, DT_BLK, DT_FIFO, DT_SOCK, DT_UNKNOWN). This is critical for ls, find, and other directory-walking tools.
acceptance_criteria_chirho: d_off values enable seeking to next entry

implementation_tasks_chirho.description_chirho: Implement reboot(magic, magic2, cmd, arg). Requires CAP_SYS_BOOT. Commands: LINUX_REBOOT_CMD_RESTART (reboot), LINUX_REBOOT_CMD_HALT (halt), LINUX_REBOOT_CMD_POWER_OFF (power off via ACPI S5), LINUX_REBOOT_CMD_RESTART2 (reboot with command string), LINUX_REBOOT_CMD_CAD_ON/OFF (Ctrl-Alt-Del handling). Magic numbers must match (LINUX_REBOOT_MAGIC1=0xfee1dead, LINUX_REBOOT_MAGIC2=0x28121969).
acceptance_criteria_chirho: reboot with correct magic numbers works
Magic number validation prevents accidental reboot

testing_strategy_chirho.overview_chirho: Multi-layered testing approach: unit tests for individual components, integration tests via QEMU, compatibility tests via Linux Test Project (LTP), and real-world application tests.

unit_testing_chirho.framework_chirho: Custom #[test_case] framework for no_std kernel code. Tests run inside QEMU with test runner that reports results via serial port exit code.

coverage_targets_chirho.mm_chirho: Page allocator, VMA operations, COW, page table manipulation
coverage_targets_chirho.vfs_chirho: Path resolution, dentry cache, inode operations
coverage_targets_chirho.sched_chirho: Task creation, scheduling decisions, priority calculations
coverage_targets_chirho.syscall_chirho: Each syscall handler tested in isolation with mock data
coverage_targets_chirho.net_chirho: Packet parsing, checksum computation, TCP state machine transitions

integration_testing_chirho.framework_chirho: QEMU with serial I/O scripting (expect-like). Each phase has a dedicated test suite.

test_suites_chirho.description_chirho: Verify kernel boots, serial output works, no panics
Static ELF hello world runs and outputs expected string
BusyBox init boots, shell responds to commands
Bash/dash job control works (bg, fg, Ctrl-Z, signals)
ext4 mount, file create, reboot, verify persistence
OCI container runs with namespace isolation
bzImage format loads via GRUB2, SMP boots
Alpine Linux userspace boots and runs

ltp_testing_chirho.description_chirho: Linux Test Project (LTP) provides thousands of test cases for Linux syscalls and features.
ltp_testing_chirho.setup_chirho: Cross-compile LTP with musl for static linking, include in test initramfs.

busybox_test_suite_chirho.description_chirho: BusyBox has its own test suite (busybox testsuite) covering all applets.

docker_test_chirho.description_chirho: Run Docker hello-world container as the Phase 7 acceptance test.
docker_test_chirho.method_chirho: Use runc directly with pre-extracted OCI bundle (avoid full Docker daemon initially).
docker_test_chirho.success_criteria_chirho: Container starts, prints 'Hello from Docker!', exits cleanly with namespaces and cgroups active.

performance_benchmarks_chirho.syscall_latency_chirho: Measure getpid(), write(), read() latency. Target: within 10% of Linux.
performance_benchmarks_chirho.context_switch_chirho: Measure context switch time via pipe ping-pong. Target: within 20% of Linux.
performance_benchmarks_chirho.network_throughput_chirho: iperf3 TCP throughput. Target: within 30% of Linux initially.
performance_benchmarks_chirho.filesystem_iops_chirho: fio random read/write IOPS on ext4. Target: within 25% of Linux.
performance_benchmarks_chirho.boot_time_chirho: Time from QEMU start to shell prompt. Target: <2 seconds.

ralph_loop_config_chirho.description_chirho: Configuration for the automated ralph loop agent that implements tasks sequentially from the PRD.

algorithm_chirho: 2. Filter tasks where all depends_on_chirho tasks have status_chirho == 'done'
3. Sort eligible tasks by: (a) phase_chirho ascending, (b) priority_chirho weight (critical=4, high=3, medium=2, low=1) descending, (c) id_chirho ascending (natural order within phase)
4. Select the first task from sorted list

steps_chirho: 1. Read the task's description_chirho, acceptance_criteria_chirho, linux_reference_files_chirho
2. If linux_reference_files_chirho is non-empty, read those files from spec-chirho/linux-reference-chirho/linux-6.19.8/ to understand the Linux implementation
3. Create or modify files listed in files_to_create_chirho and files_to_modify_chirho
4. Follow CLAUDE.md naming conventions (all identifiers end with Chirho suffix)
5. Add John 3:16 comment at top of all new files
6. Write unit tests for new code where applicable
7. Run cargo build to verify compilation
8. If the task has a corresponding QEMU test, run it
9. Verify each acceptance criterion is met
10. Update task status_chirho to 'done' in the PRD JSON
on_compilation_error_chirho: 2. Fix the issue (type error, missing import, etc.)
4. If stuck after 3 attempts, mark task status_chirho as 'blocked' with a note and move to next eligible task
on_test_failure_chirho: 2. Debug using serial output / QEMU monitor
5. If stuck after 5 attempts, mark task as 'blocked' and continue

validation_chirho.clippy_check_chirho: cargo clippy --target x86_64-unknown-none must pass with zero warnings
validation_chirho.test_check_chirho: cargo xtask test-phase{current_phase} must pass (if phase test exists)
validation_chirho.acceptance_check_chirho: All acceptance_criteria_chirho items verified (self-assessed by agent, logged to progress DB)

iteration_limits_chirho.pause_action_chirho: Stop and report blocked tasks to user for manual intervention

phase_gates_chirho.description_chirho: Before moving to the next phase, ALL critical tasks in the current phase must be 'done' and the phase integration test must pass.
gate_checks_chirho: All tasks with priority_chirho 'critical' for the phase are 'done'
Phase integration test passes (cargo xtask test-phase{N})
No regressions in previous phase tests
Code compiles with zero clippy warnings
